scope: M10-M12 (47 slides) LT + EN, plus glossary, locales, handout and lab TS copy

reviewFindings.citation: "Incidentų planas: sustabdyti → fiksuoti → įvertinti → pranešti → ištaisyti (žr. **Minimalus eigos aprašymas**)."
reviewFindings.problem: five LT fields on `123` send the learner to **Minimalus eigos aprašymas** (`10.64`) for the 5-step incident plan. `10.64` does not contain an incident plan — its three blocks are A flow, B three tests, C human decision (`10.64` `content.sections[1].body`: "**C. Žmogaus sprendimas:** kada stabdyti, kas tvirtina ir ką užfiksuoti."). The plan lives on `10.65` (`content.sections[2].body`: "**5 žingsniai:** sustabdyti → fiksuoti → įvertinti → pranešti → ištaisyti."). The source of truth is explicit that this is intentional slide ownership, not a naming variant — `docs/turinio_pletra_moduliai_10_11_12.md` line 522: "Incidentų planas ir modelio kainos gilinimas priklauso 10.65." A learner who follows the pointer lands on a slide that cannot answer the request.
reviewFindings.direction: repoint all five fields at the slide that owns the artifact. Because that slide is optional (X1-02), the pointer alone is not sufficient — pair it with the inline 5-step list already present in `practicalTask.template` so the practice is self-sufficient.

reviewFindings.problem: a required artifact of a completion-counted practice is produced only on a slide the learner is told they may skip. The path overview markets `10.65` as skippable — `10.1` `content.sections[0].body`: "**Neprivaloma:** GitHub, gilesnė specifikacija, žodynėlis, santrauka." A learner on the short path reaches `123` having never seen the incident plan, and `123` gives them no way to build one.
reviewFindings.direction: either promote the 5-step incident plan into the MUST path (a 3-line block on `10.64` alongside part C would carry it), or make `123`'s template self-contained so the optional slide is genuinely optional. Do not leave a required input behind an optional gate.

reviewFindings.path: slide 10.482 — no copyable field exists anywhere on the slide; content.sections[2].body
reviewFindings.citation: "Pereik visus 6 žingsnius. Žingsnyje **Klaida ir KARTOTI** pastebėk **KARTOTI** kilpą"
reviewFindings.problem: `10.482` is a MUST slide with a strong diagram and a genuine conceptual payload (router ≠ orchestrator; checker ≠ evaluator; targeted retry). Its "Daryk dabar" asks the learner to walk the diagram and its "Patikra" asks two recall questions with no fallback (`content.sections[3].body`: "Vienu sakiniu: kuo **maršrutizatorius** (KUR) skiriasi nuo **orkestratoriaus** (KAIP)?"). Nothing written leaves the slide. It sits immediately before the `10.481` section-break, so the learner produces no output across two consecutive slides — and the router/orchestrator distinction is then tested in M11 (`docs/turinio_pletra_moduliai_10_11_12.md` line 789: "router ≠ orkestratorius (10.482 / 10.485)").
reviewFindings.direction: give the slide one short artifact so the distinction survives the slide — for example a 3-line "my process: where is the router decision, where is the orchestrator decision, what does a targeted retry return" prompt. The GOLDEN §3.2 contract (Trumpai → Daryk dabar → Kopijuojamas promptas → Patikra) already expects the copy step here.

reviewFindings.path: 121 practicalTask.instructions.steps[1].description / .hint / .partialSolution; same triplet on 121 steps 2 and 3, 123 steps 1 and 2, 124 step 0
reviewFindings.problem: 7 of the 11 steps that have a hint carry the identical string in `description`, `hint` and `partialSolution`. The UI offers a three-rung escalation and all three rungs return the same sentence, so a stuck learner who clicks twice learns nothing and has no reason to trust the affordance again. This hits hardest on `121`, the first mandatory practice: 4 of 4 steps have `description` = `hint`, 3 of 4 are fully collapsed. `122` shows the intended shape and proves the fix is cheap — step 0 runs description → "Jei neturi DI modulio, sugeneruok platformos specifikaciją su ChatGPT: moduliai, promptas, tvirtinimas, testai." → "Be paskyros užtenka dokumento su triggeriu, santraukos promptu, tvirtinimo taisykle ir testais."
reviewFindings.direction: apply the `122` step-0 pattern across all collapsed steps — `description` states the task, `hint` names the constraint or the slide to reuse, `partialSolution` shows a filled fragment. Consider a lint that fails when the three fields on a step are equal.

reviewFindings.path: practicalTask.instructions.steps[0..3] — .hint and .partialSolution absent on all four steps
reviewFindings.problem: `124.5` is a MUST slide and the recommended entry point into M12 (`120` `content.pathChoices[0].description`: "3A orientyras → schema → kontrolinis taškas → greitas startas → 3 privalomos praktikos."). It is also the only slide that produces the Įgūdžio paketas the summary counts. Its four steps have no hint and no partial solution at all, so the most structurally demanding step on the slide — assembling a 7-field reusable skill pack — offers a single sentence of guidance and no way down.
reviewFindings.direction: add hint and partialSolution to step 3 at minimum, seeded from the skill-pack block already present in `practicalTask.template`.

reviewFindings.problem: all three templates are 30–34-word forms consisting only of labelled blanks. None contains a verb addressed to the AI, and the section body confirms the intent is a form, not a prompt (`content.sections[4].body`: "Užpildyk [ ] laukus. Režimas jau pažymėtas."). They are labelled "Kopijuojamas šablonas" and sit directly after `10.35`, whose four templates are 78–101-word Flagship prompts with a role, a numbered output contract and a clarifying-question rule ("Grąžink lentelėmis. Jei trūksta informacijos, pirma paklausk iki 3 klausimų."). Adjacent slides teaching two incompatible ideas of what a copyable is.
reviewFindings.direction: either add a closing request so the AI does something with the form — `10.37`'s optional template already models this ("Patikrink mano pasirinkimą 3 eilutėmis. Jei pasirinkimas per sudėtingas, pasiūlyk paprastesnį kelią.") — or relabel these as a decision worksheet rather than a copyable prompt. `10.25` handles the same tension honestly by saying "Nukopijuok šabloną į DI arba užsirašyk".

reviewFindings.problem: the five pattern plans are genuinely different (chain, routing, parallel, coordinator, generator + evaluator — 22–28 words each and correctly differentiated), but the instruction line above each is the same five-word sentence. Since the UI reveals only the selected pattern's plan, the learner sees a generic instruction where a pattern-specific one would tell them what they are about to produce. This is the visible half of a deeper issue: none of the five plans is referenced again anywhere on the path (§3).
reviewFindings.direction: give each of the five bodies one differentiating clause naming the plan's output, and add a downstream consumer — the natural one is `10.64`, whose part A ("Veiksmai (3–5)") is exactly what the chosen pattern plan produces.

reviewFindings.problem: at 11, 14 and 16 words these are the three shortest copyables on the 47-slide path, and they are positioned as the module-10 recap *after* the learner has completed three graded practices. `sections[4].copyable` is a shortened restatement of `10.6` `content.sections[2].copyable` (24 words). The recap therefore represents M10 at roughly a fifth of the maturity M10 actually taught (`10.5` at 84 words, `10.35` at 99–101).
reviewFindings.direction: the slide is optional and low-friction by design, which is fine — but a recap should point back at the artifacts, not re-issue beginner prompts. Replace the three stubs with one prompt that asks the learner to re-run their own `10.64` brief or `10.5` agent prompt and name one thing to change.

reviewFindings.path: no Patikra / check field exists on any of the five; the closest field is scenario.expectedFormat
reviewFindings.problem: every M10 content-block closes with a Patikra and most name a fallback — `10.15` "Jei ne – pataisyk šabloną pagal pavyzdį."; `10.2` "Jei ne – grįžk į diagramą."; `120.25` "Jei juosta neaiški – grįžk į M10 **„3A strategija“** prieš praktiką." The five practice slides, where the learner is doing the hardest work and is most likely to produce something incomplete, close with an artifact inventory and no pass/fail rule and no remediation target. `expectedFormat` tells the learner what to hand in, not whether what they made is good enough or where to go if it is not.
reviewFindings.direction: add a two-question gate plus one fallback target to each practice, reusing targets that already exist: `121` → `10.64`; `122` → `10.26` (its LT step-1 hint already points there); `123` → the incident-plan slide once X1-01 is fixed.

reviewFindings.path: 10.5 content.sections[2].body; 10.51 content.body; absence of any reference on 121, 122, 123
reviewFindings.problem: M10 twice tells the learner that the 84-word Flagship agent prompt and its golden edge-case check exist specifically for M12 practice, and gives it a dedicated checkpoint (`10.51`) and a quality evaluator (`10.66`). No M12 practice asks for it. `121` asks for a workflow spec form, `122` for a summary prompt, `123` for thresholds. The most mature prompt the course teaches is built, checkpointed, evaluated — and then never cashed in.
reviewFindings.direction: have at least one mandatory practice require the `10.5` prompt as an input, the way `123` requires the `10.64` brief. `122` is the natural host: its summary prompt is currently the thinnest part of a 79-word template and would benefit from role, tools, format and error-handling blocks.

reviewFindings.problem: `121` tells the learner to reuse the `10.64` structure and then supplies a 32-word template that is a reduction of it: 2 tests instead of 3, and no part C at all. `10.64` teaches three tests ("**B. Trys bandymai:** sėkmės kelias, trūkstamas laukas ir neatsakanti arba pasikartojanti sistema.") and a human-decision block, and its own Patikra asks for all three parts. The source of truth backs the three-test requirement — `docs/turinio_pletra_moduliai_10_11_12.md` line 969: "**Testavimo rinkinys (minimalus)** … **10.64** (3 bandymo atvejai MUST)". The first graded practice therefore accepts less than the MUST slide required.
reviewFindings.direction: align `121`'s template with `10.64` A/B/C — a third test row and a human-decision line — or state explicitly why the Automatize band drops part C.

reviewFindings.citation: "Parašyk min. 2 bandymo atvejus ir padaryk logų / ekrano nuotraukų"
reviewFindings.problem: the no-account fallback is stated clearly at scenario level and in step 0 ("arba parenk vedamąjį dokumentą"), and `scenario.expectedFormat` accepts "dokumento ištraukos". Step 3 was not updated: its title and description ("Sėkmingas paleidimas + vienas klaidos atvejis.") both assume a real run in a real platform. An account-free learner reaches the last step of the first mandatory practice and is asked for screenshots of something they never ran.
reviewFindings.direction: mirror step 0's phrasing — "…arba užrašyk laukiamą rezultatą kiekvienam bandymui vedamajame dokumente".

reviewFindings.problem: the Įgūdžio paketas block is present in the LT `practicalTask.template` (pavadinimas / kada naudoti / rolės / žingsniai / ribos / patikra / pamoka) and absent from the EN template, which ends at EVALUATOR. EN step 3 is boilerplate. The source of truth lists the skill pack as a required artifact of this slide (`docs/turinio_pletra_moduliai_10_11_12.md` line 911: "**Artefaktai:** schema + 3 promptai + 1 bandymo atvejis + **Įgūdžio paketas**"). The EN summary has already been reworded around the gap, so the EN learner never learns the artifact exists.
reviewFindings.direction: port the skill-pack block and step-3 copy into the EN overlay and into `build-en-m10-m12.mjs`, then restore the EN stat to match.

reviewFindings.problem: within a single step, the EN description points at one slide and the EN hint and partialSolution point at a different one. The hint is the correct target (Testing and security = `10.65`, which owns the incident plan); the description is not. LT has the same three fields all pointing at the wrong slide (X1-01). Resolving X1-01 must settle both languages on one target rather than fixing them independently.
reviewFindings.direction: fold into X1-01 and set one target for LT and EN.

reviewFindings.problem: `10.26`'s lab explicitly generates a human-control rule destined for the `10.64` brief, and `10.26`'s Patikra names the handoff again ("Ar tavo „Minimalus eigos aprašymas“ žmogaus patvirtinimo eilutėje bus režimas, sąlyga, eskalacija ir audito įrašas?"). `10.64` never mentions `10.26` or that output — its part C reads as a fresh fill-in, so a learner who generated the rule 19 slides earlier has no cue to paste it. The only slide that closes the loop is `122`'s LT step-1 hint, and the EN hint drops the pointer. The source of truth treats this as one designed chain (line 970: "**10.26** režimų simuliatorius → HITL eilutė **10.64**").
reviewFindings.direction: one clause in `10.64` part C naming the `10.26` output ("įklijuok taisyklę iš **Kada tvirtina žmogus?**"), and restore the pointer in the `122` EN hint.

reviewFindings.target: slides 10.61 + 111 — graded 3A item duplicates the warm-up 3A item
reviewFindings.citation: "Kuris 3A pasirinkimas tinka procesui, kuriame taisyklės aiškios, rizika maža, o žmogaus sprendimo beveik nereikia?" / "Procesas kartojasi kiekvieną dieną: … rizika maža, o žmogus beveik nieko nesprendžia."
reviewFindings.problem: Same concept, same cue words, same correct answer ("Automatizuoti"), and a byte-identical option list in identical order: `Automatizuoti`, `Asistuoti`, `Autonomizuoti`, `Neautomatizuoti`. The explanations also converge — warm-up: "Automatizuoti tinka aiškioms, pasikartojančioms, mažos rizikos taisyklėms."; graded: "Tai aiškus, pasikartojantis, mažos rizikos procesas." A learner who did `10.61` can answer `111 q[1]` from recall of the option list alone, so the item measures nothing. The overlap is drift, not design: SOT §4.4a specifies the three `10.61` questions as "Nepavyko pranešimas; kada agentas vs promptas; paieškos / įrankio cue" — no 3A item — and the live LT subtitle still reads "3 klausimai: klaidos tvarkymas, agentas, paieška" while the EN subtitle already says "error handling, 3A, search".
reviewFindings.direction: Restore `10.61 q[1]` to the SOT-specified agent-vs-prompt cue, or re-cast the graded item so the correct band is not Automatizuoti and the option list differs. Whichever moves, the option lists must stop matching.

reviewFindings.target: slides 110.5 + 111 — pre-test warm-up previews the graded artifact item
reviewFindings.citation: "Vieną 5 dalių agentinį promptą ir minimalios darbo eigos aprašymo karkasą" / "Minimalus darbo eigos aprašymas: triggeris, įvesties schema, veiksmai, klaidos, testai ir žmogaus kontrolė"
reviewFindings.problem: `110.5` is the slide immediately before `111`. Both ask which artifact to prepare first, both have the minimal workflow brief as the correct answer, and the distractor families mirror each other ("Tik platformos paskyra be bandymo atvejų" / "Tik platformos pasirinkimas be laukų"; "Tik ilgą teorinį paaiškinimą be proceso" / "Tik vienas bendras promptas be testų"). This is also drift: SOT §7.1a specifies the three `110.5` questions as "agentas vs promptas; 3A Asistuoti juosta; router ≠ orkestratorius (10.482 / 10.485)" — the artifact question replaced the router item. Combined with X2-01, X2-03 and X2-04, 4 of 9 graded items are pre-answered on formative slides against a ≥70 % (7 of 9) pass bar.
reviewFindings.direction: Return `110.5 q[2]` to the router ≠ orchestrator item the SOT specifies; it is the one M10 distinction the test never probes, so the swap fixes a leak and a coverage gap at once.

reviewFindings.target: slides 10.22 + 10.61 + 111 — error handling asked three times, the graded item is the third
reviewFindings.citation: "Ką agentas turi grąžinti, jei įrankio naudoti negali?" / "Koks geras rezultatas, kai DI negali atlikti užduoties?" / "Ką daryti, kai agentas negali atlikti užduoties?"
reviewFindings.problem: Three stems, one concept. `10.61 q[0]`'s correct option ("Aiškus „Nepavyko: [priežastis]“ ir pasiūlymas, ką pataisyti") and `111 q[3]`'s correct option ("Nurodyti sisteminiame arba vartotojo prompte: parašyti „Nepavyko“ ir priežastį") differ only by naming the prompt layer. Distractors repeat across all three ("Tuščias atsakymas", "Kartoti tą patį promptą"). On top of the three questions, the same rule ships as a copyable on `10.5`, `10.6`, `10.51`, `10.65` and `125` (16 statements total, see §5).
reviewFindings.direction: Keep one formative ask (`10.22 q[2]`, closest to where the rule is taught) and make the graded item diagnostic instead of recall — e.g. give a failing agent output and ask which of four error-handling clauses is missing.

reviewFindings.target: slides 10.61 + 111 — "use search, provide sources" rule asked twice, correct option reused
reviewFindings.citation: "„Naudok paiešką ir pateik šaltinius“" / "Aiškiai nurodyti įrankį ir taisyklę: naudok paiešką, pateik šaltinius, jei nerandi – parašyk „Nerasta“"
reviewFindings.problem: The graded correct option is the warm-up correct option plus a "Nerasta" clause. The scenario wrapper ("DI agentas pateikia užtikrintą atsakymą, bet nenurodo šaltinių") is the only new content, so the item tests scenario reading rather than the rule. The rule is additionally stated at `10.4 content.sections[2].body` and `10.8 content.firstAction24h`.
reviewFindings.direction: Since the graded item is the better-built of the two, drop or repoint `10.61 q[2]`; the slide already covers error handling and 3A in its other items.

reviewFindings.target: EN overlay — one boilerplate sentence 12×, leaving mandatory EN slides empty
reviewFindings.path: 10.26 content.sections[0].body, [1].body, [2].body (EN) and 10.451 content.body, content.sections[0].body, content.sections[1].body (EN); also 100 content.howToUseModule.short.description + full.description, 10.21 content.body + sections[0].body + sections[1].body, 124.5 practicalTask.instructions.steps[3].description
reviewFindings.citation: "Use this step to design, test and improve an AI agent workflow with clear tools, limits and human approval" / (LT counterpart on 10.26) "Žmogaus kontrolė (pramonėje – **Human-in-the-loop / HITL**) nėra brandos kopėčios iki autopiloto."
reviewFindings.problem: Verified 12 occurrences of the identical sentence in `src/data/modules-en-m10-m12.json`. This is not a translation issue — it is the same EN string repeated where different EN content belongs. `10.26` and `10.451` are mandatory slides whose every body field is this sentence, so for an EN learner both slides teach nothing and read as a copy-paste error. Two sibling fillers compound it: "AI agent workflow step." (18×) and, in the glossary, "A key term used in agent engineering." (5×).
reviewFindings.direction: Treat the three fillers as a single EN overlay debt item and translate the LT bodies for `10.26`, `10.451`, `10.21` and `100` first, since those are mandatory-path slides. Patch `scripts/build-en-m10-m12.mjs` alongside the JSON or a rebuild will reinstate the placeholders.

reviewFindings.target: M12 practice scenarios — every EN template exists twice in the same slide
reviewFindings.path: 124 practicalTask.template and 124 content.template; same pairing on 121, 122, 123, 124.5
reviewFindings.citation: "You are a research agent with a source-quality rule." (both fields) / "COORDINATOR: You are the coordinator. Task: [DESCRIBE]. Break into 2 sub-tasks, assign roles, handoff rules."
reviewFindings.problem: Verified 2 occurrences of the research-agent opener in the EN file, both on slide `124`. The legacy `content.*` block mirrors `practicalTask.*` byte for byte across `template`, `templateLabel`, `instructions.title` and every `instructions.steps[*]` — roughly 40 duplicated EN fields across the five practice scenarios. The LT side has none of these (`LT: (none)` throughout), so every future EN copy edit has to be made twice or the two will silently diverge.
reviewFindings.direction: Confirm which shape the renderer reads for `practice-scenario`, then delete the unused mirror rather than maintaining both.

reviewFindings.target: M12 practices — hint and partialSolution are copies of description
reviewFindings.path: 121 practicalTask.instructions.steps[1..3], 122 …steps[2], 123 …steps[1..2], 124 …steps[0] — in each case .description, .hint and .partialSolution hold one string
reviewFindings.citation: "Naudok struktūrą kaip **Minimalus eigos aprašymas** (trigger → klaidos + 2 bandymai)." / "Užpildyk [TEMA] ir [AUDITORIJA]. Paleisk ir peržiūrėk šaltinių lentelę."
reviewFindings.problem: `hint` and `partialSolution` are progressive-disclosure affordances. Filling them with the description means a stuck learner who asks for a hint, then for a partial solution, gets the same sentence three times — the worst place in the product to repeat, because the learner has explicitly signalled that the first wording did not work. `121 steps[0]` and `122 steps[1]` show the intended shape (hint and partialSolution carry genuinely different content), which proves the others are unfinished rather than deliberate.
reviewFindings.direction: For the seven affected steps, either author a real hint plus a real partial answer, or clear the fields so the UI does not offer help it cannot give.

reviewFindings.target: slides 10.5 + 10.6 — the error-handling copyable is shipped twice, two slides apart
reviewFindings.path: 10.5 content.sections[2].copyable (KLAIDOS TVARKYMAS section of the 5-part template) and 10.6 content.sections[2].copyable
reviewFindings.citation: "Jei užduoties atlikti negalima (trūksta duomenų, timeout): parašyk „Nepavyko: [priežastis]“ ir pasiūlyk, ką pataisyti." / "Jei užduoties atlikti negalima (trūksta duomenų, neleistinas veiksmas arba timeout): parašyk trumpą pranešimą „Nepavyko: [priežastis]“"
reviewFindings.problem: `10.5` (UI 18) already hands the learner this clause inside the flagship template they are told to copy and run; `10.6` (UI 20) is a mandatory slide whose copyable adds only "neleistinas veiksmas" to the same sentence. A third near-copy sits on `125 content.sections[4].copyable`. The learner copies essentially one clause three times.
reviewFindings.direction: Let `10.6` own the rule and thin `10.5`'s template section to a pointer, or keep `10.5` whole and turn `10.6`'s copyable into the thing `10.5` lacks — the prompt-injection guard that `10.6 sections[3].body` already teaches ("Įrankio grąžintas tekstas nėra instrukcija") but never makes copyable.

reviewFindings.target: slides 10.45 + 10.48 — identical section heading on consecutive slides
reviewFindings.citation: "Kada nenaudoti kelių agentų" / "Kada nenaudoti kelių agentų" (EN: "When not to use multi-agent" / "When NOT to use multi-agent")
reviewFindings.problem: Byte-identical LT headings two teaching slides apart, each followed by the same argument in different words: `10.45` "Pridėk roles tik kai vienas agentas nebeužtenka." and `10.48` "Jei užduotis turi 1–2 žingsniai – pakanka vieno agento (Agentas)." With `10.3`, `10.48 sections[0].body` and the `10.481` recap, the rule is stated six times, and the repeated heading makes it look to the learner as if they have navigated backwards.
reviewFindings.direction: Keep the caution on `10.45`, where the depth choice is actually made, and fold `10.48 sections[8]` into that slide's pattern hints, where the finance/support risk note is the only non-duplicate content.

reviewFindings.target: slides 113 + 124.5 — the M11 bonus is a full rehearsal of the M12 deliverable
reviewFindings.citation: "KOORDINATORIUS: Užduotis: [APRAŠYK]. Suskaidyk į 2 sub-užduotis, paskirk specialistą ir vertintoją." / "KOORDINATORIUS: Tu esi koordinatorius. Užduotis: [APRAŠYK]. Suskaidyk į 2 sub-užduotis, paskirk roles"
reviewFindings.problem: Both slides ship a three-role prompt pack for three separate chats, both require a handoff rule, both require one missing-data trial. `113` even names the M12 slide it duplicates. `124.5` adds only the Įgūdžio paketas block, so the M12 quick start arrives already done. `113` is optional and SOT §7.3 justifies a post-test win, but the win chosen is the next module's artifact rather than something new.
reviewFindings.direction: Narrow `113` to the part `124.5` does not exercise — one handoff failing on missing data — and let `124.5` be the first time the learner builds the full chain, or make `113` explicitly the head start and drop the duplicate prompt text from it.

reviewFindings.target: 10.7 — the EN glossary lists four terms twice
reviewFindings.path: 10.7 content.terms[12].term / terms[18].term (EN), and the same pattern at terms[13]/terms[19], terms[14]/terms[20], terms[15]/terms[21]
reviewFindings.citation: "Coordinator" with "Multi-agent role – breaks down task, delegates to specialists, merges results." / "Coordinator" with "A key term used in agent engineering."
reviewFindings.problem: In EN the glossary shows Coordinator, Evaluator, Router and ReAct twice each — once with a real definition and once with the placeholder. The cause is visible in the corpus: the EN term array is offset against LT from `terms[7]` onward, so EN definitions no longer sit under their LT terms and the tail is padded. A glossary that lists a term twice with different content is worse than one that omits it, since the learner cannot tell which entry to trust.
reviewFindings.direction: Re-align the EN `terms[]` array to LT index by index and delete the five placeholder definitions; the real EN definitions for all four roles already exist earlier in the same array.

reviewFindings.target: 123 — the five-step incident playbook is repeated five times and points at the wrong slide
reviewFindings.citation: "Incidentų planas: sustabdyti → fiksuoti → įvertinti → pranešti → ištaisyti (žr. **Minimalus eigos aprašymas**)." / "5 žingsniai: sustabdyti, fiksuoti, įvertinti, pranešti, ištaisyti – skaidrė **Minimalus eigos aprašymas**."
reviewFindings.problem: Two defects in one place. The five steps appear five times on a single slide. And the pointer is wrong: `10.64` (Minimalus darbo eigos aprašymas) never mentions an incident playbook — it lives on `10.65 content.sections[2].body` "**5 žingsniai:** sustabdyti → fiksuoti → įvertinti → pranešti → ištaisyti", which is an optional slide. The EN version of the same fields already points to "Testing and security", i.e. `10.65`, so LT and EN disagree about where the learner should look, and a learner on the mandatory path was never shown the playbook at all.
reviewFindings.direction: State the five steps once on `123`, fix the LT pointer to `10.65`, and — since `123` is a mandatory practice that depends on it — decide whether the playbook must move onto the mandatory path.

reviewFindings.target: 10.481 — the recap credits a taxonomy label the teaching slide never used
reviewFindings.citation: "Gylis L0–L3 – kada pakanka vieno agento, kada reikia kelių." / "Pokalbis, agentas, komanda ar automatinis srautas"
reviewFindings.problem: The recap tells the learner they know "L0–L3", but the depth slide teaches named depths only, and `10.8 content.introBody` reinforces the names ("agentų gylis (Pokalbis → Srautas)"). L0–L3 survives only in `100 content.outcomes[0]`, in bare "L1 / L2" references on `10.451` and `10.48`, and in `111 testQuestions[5].explanation`. The SOT still carries the L-coded table (§ taxonomy table, rows L0–L3), so this is residue from the rename to named depths.
reviewFindings.direction: Either drop the codes from `10.481` and the stray L1/L2 mentions, or reintroduce the mapping once on `10.45` so the codes have an anchor.

reviewFindings.target: slides 10.48 + 10.36 — identical copy-lead-in lines repeated 5× and 3×
reviewFindings.citation: "Nukopijuok ir užpildyk [APRAŠYK]." / "Užpildyk [ ] laukus. Režimas jau pažymėtas."
reviewFindings.problem: Verified 5 occurrences of the `10.48` line in `src/data/modules.json`. Because both slides gate their sections behind a `toolChoiceBar`, a learner sees only one at a time, so the cost is authoring debt rather than learner time. Worth noting because the previous audit described these as duplicated "Daryk dabar" text; they are in fact the copyable lead-in bodies, and on `10.36` the three copyables behind them are themselves ~90 % identical, differing only in the `Režimas:` line.
reviewFindings.direction: No learner-facing fix needed. If these ever become simultaneously visible, collapse to one lead-in above the choice bar.

reviewFindings.target: 10.65 — the three QC tests are printed twice on one slide
reviewFindings.citation: "(1) Tuščia įvestis – ar grąžina aiškų „Nepavyko“?" / "(1) Tuščia įvestis – ar grąžina „Nepavyko“?"
reviewFindings.problem: The same three tests appear inside the copyable checklist and again as a standalone section on the same slide, differing by one word. The slide is optional and already the densest in M10 (49 text fields, 3039 LT chars), so the second copy costs budget on the slide least able to spare it.
reviewFindings.direction: Drop `sections[8]`; the copyable already carries the tests in the form the learner will use.

reviewFindings.target: slides 10.482 + 120.5 — the multi-agent chain crosses modules, but the second pass earns its place
reviewFindings.citation: "Agentų orkestravimo srautas: įvestis, maršrutizatorius, orkestratorius, specialistai … vertintojas, rezultatas" / "įvestis → maršrutizatorius (pasirenkama) → koordinatorius → specialistai → vertintojas → išvestis"
reviewFindings.problem: The chain is genuinely restated one module later, as the prior audit suspected, and `120.55 content.sections[0].body` states it a third time in the next slide. But `120.5` scopes itself explicitly in `content.whyBenefit` ("Pilną orkestravimo eigą matei skaidrėje **Agentų orkestravimo simuliacija** – čia tik praktikos žemėlapis ir perdavimo taisyklė") and delivers content `10.482` does not have: the JSON handoff contract with `quality_gate` and `human_review` fields.
reviewFindings.direction: No content change. The compressible part is `120.55`, whose "Ką patikrinti" repeats the chain a third time in two slides; the checkpoint could test the handoff rule instead of re-listing roles.

reviewFindings.target: 10.66 — title and template label are the same string
reviewFindings.citation: "Žingsniai: vertintojas tikrina tavo specifikaciją" / "Žingsniai: vertintojas tikrina tavo specifikaciją"
reviewFindings.problem: Byte-identical, so the heading renders twice above the same block. The steps in `practicalTask.template` also restate `content.sections[1].body` ("Nukopijuok vertintoją, įklijuok savo agentinį promptą … ir pataisyk bent vieną vietą") as a numbered list.
reviewFindings.direction: Give the label the artifact name ("Vertintojo žingsniai") or leave it empty.

reviewFindings.target: 10.8 — the summary presents twelve use cases the module never showed
reviewFindings.citation: "HR: naujas darbuotojas → onboarding checklistas → praleistas žingsnis → completion rate" / "Pritaikymo pavyzdžiai" (value 12)
reviewFindings.problem: None of the twelve rows appears on any M10–12 slide — searching all eight batches for `onboarding`, `OCR`, `shortlist` and `biudžeto nuokrypis` returns matches only inside `10.8`. They are sanctioned by SOT §6 as a "Pritaikymo katalogas (12 eilučių – santraukoje matomas grid)", so this is deliberate new material rather than accidental duplication; the defect is only that it sits under the heading "Ką išmokai" and is counted as a learning statistic.
reviewFindings.direction: Keep the catalogue, reframe the block as "Kur pritaikyti" and drop it from the "Ką išmokai" stats, so the summary does not claim credit for content the learner has not seen.

reviewFindings.citation: "Use this step to design, test and improve an AI agent workflow with clear tools, limits and human approval where needed."
reviewFindings.problem: All three EN section bodies on this slide (`sections[0].body`, `sections[1].body`, `sections[2].body`) carry the same generic build fallback sentence. The EN learner never learns the slide's actual thesis (human control = risk architecture: consequence × reversibility), never gets the instruction to pick a scenario and a control mode, and gets no gate question. The EN version of a MUST slide teaches nothing, and the same string is reused elsewhere in the overlay, so the learner also sees it as noise.
reviewFindings.direction: Author real EN copy for all three bodies from the LT source and the SOT thesis; audit the EN build script's fallback so a missing translation fails loudly instead of emitting a plausible-looking generic sentence.

reviewFindings.citation: "Role: agent assistant. Task: review the process, use tools only when needed, return a clear result and say what failed if data is missing."
reviewFindings.problem: The EN copyable is a different prompt from LT, not a translation. LT hands the learner a task template with a fill-in slot and a 3-part answer contract ("ką darei, kokį įrankį naudojai, koks rezultatas"); EN gives a generic role/persona prompt with no slot to fill and no required answer shape. The checkpoint asks the learner to verify steps and a tool trace in the output, but the EN prompt does not ask the model to produce them, so the EN learner cannot pass their own check.
reviewFindings.direction: Translate the LT copyable, keeping the fill-in slot and the three required answer parts; the same generic role prompt also appears on the sibling checkpoint, so fix the pattern, not just this instance.

reviewFindings.citation: "Use this step to design, test and improve an AI agent workflow with clear tools, limits and human approval where needed."
reviewFindings.problem: The EN step body and both EN section bodies ("Check", "If it fails") use the same generic fallback. LT tells the learner exactly what to run and when to mark the step done, plus concrete repair sentences to add if the run fails ("naudok paiešką", "pateik šaltinius"). In EN there is no instruction, no completion criterion and no recovery path, so a path-step that is meant to be markable becomes unmarkable in practice.
reviewFindings.direction: Translate the LT body, the "Check" questions and the "If it fails" repair sentences; keep the checkpoint's markable criterion explicit in EN.

reviewFindings.citation: "**MUST kelias:** agentų ciklas → 3A strategija → gylis ir rolės → 5 darbo eigos šablonai → rolė ir sisteminis promptas"
reviewFindings.problem: This is the learner's map of the module, and it does not match the module. It omits the two MUST slides that come immediately next ("Ar komanda pasirengusi agentiniam darbui?" and "Kada tvirtina žmogus?"), omits the closed learning loop, and omits "Minimalus darbo eigos aprašymas" — the slide that produces the module's main artifact and is referenced later from M12. It also states the order wrongly: "rolė ir sisteminis promptas" is listed after the 5 patterns, but in the live sequence the system-prompt slide comes before depth/roles and before the patterns. A learner who uses this list to plan or to skip will trust a stale map.
reviewFindings.direction: Regenerate the MUST chain from the official order (`docs/MODULIO_10_SKAIDRIU_EILES.md`) so every MUST slide appears once and in real order; keep item names as slide names, not curriculum IDs. Consider grouping into 3–4 stages instead of an 11-arrow chain, so the list survives future reordering.

reviewFindings.citation: "Click a step – explanation below. View full size – the same image opens in a modal."
reviewFindings.problem: EN adds a sentence that LT does not have and that the product does not deliver: interactive process diagrams render without the desktop enlarge control, so there is no modal to open. The learner looks for a control that is not there and concludes the slide is broken. This is the false "full size / modal" promise that was removed from LT but is still live in the EN overlay.
reviewFindings.direction: Delete the second sentence in EN so it mirrors LT (click a step → explanation below); check the EN build script for the same appended sentence on other diagram slides.

reviewFindings.citation: "Agent metric"
reviewFindings.problem: The path chooser is broken in EN. Both option labels read "Agent metric" (LT: "Trumpas kelias" / "Ilgas kelias"), both descriptions are the same generic fallback sentence, and the group heading is "Agent engineering step" instead of an instruction to choose. The EN learner is shown two identically labeled, identically described options and cannot tell the short path from the full one — the choice that governs how much of the module they will do.
reviewFindings.direction: Translate the LT labels, the group heading and both descriptions so short vs full is distinguishable, and list in EN exactly which slide groups the short path drops.

reviewFindings.citation: "sugeneruos taisyklę „Minimalus eigos aprašymas“ aprašymui."
reviewFindings.problem: The sentence that tells the learner what they will walk away with is the least readable one on the slide: a rule "for the description" of a quoted slide name. On top of that, "Minimalus eigos aprašymas" is a forward reference to a slide roughly twenty slides later, dropped here with no gloss of what that document is or why the learner should keep the rule. The learner cannot tell whether they are producing something they need now or something to file away.
reviewFindings.direction: Say plainly what the lab produces (a control rule: mode, condition, escalation, audit) and where it is used later, glossing the target document in words rather than quoting its title.

reviewFindings.citation: "Ar tavo „Minimalus eigos aprašymas“ žmogaus patvirtinimo eilutėje bus režimas, sąlyga, eskalacija ir audito įrašas?"
reviewFindings.problem: The gate question is close to unparseable: a quoted slide title is wedged into a possessive chain, so the reader cannot tell whose row is being asked about. It also silently requires four elements (mode, condition, escalation, audit record) that are not enumerated anywhere in this slide's own text, and the check has no fallback for a "no" answer — unlike the strong gates on the neighbouring slides.
reviewFindings.direction: Split into two short questions, name the four required elements as a visible list somewhere on the slide before the gate, and add an explicit fallback (which block to return to when an element is missing).

reviewFindings.citation: "Silpniausia dimensija parodys vieną kitą veiksmą prieš didinant autonomiją."
reviewFindings.problem: "vieną kitą veiksmą" idiomatically means "an action or two, a few" — vague and plural — while the whole point of the slide (and the EN text, "one next action") is that the weakest dimension yields exactly ONE next action. The learner is told to expect an indefinite handful of actions and therefore does not know when they are done. Note: the SOT phrases it the same way ("gauna vieną kitą veiksmą"), so the wording should be tightened in both places rather than treated as a live-vs-SOT conflict.
reviewFindings.direction: Commit to the singular ("vieną tolesnį veiksmą" style) in LT and in the SOT so LT, EN and the lab artifact ("Kitas veiksmas: [vienas veiksmas]") all promise one action.

reviewFindings.citation: "Design agents for your processes – taxonomy, multi-agent coordination, no-code tools. Context – Module 4."
reviewFindings.problem: EN loses the two things LT promises here. LT frames the first item as depth levels and roles ("gylio lygiai ir rolės"), EN calls it "taxonomy" — the internal word the SOT explicitly bans from learner UI. And LT's transfer sentence ("M4–M6 konteksto inžineriją čia taikysi agentams" — you will apply what you learned) shrinks in EN to a bare pointer, "Context – Module 4.", which reads as a prerequisite note instead of a promise. The EN outcome line drops "konteksto taisyklės agentams" the same way, and the EN duration promises less time than LT, so an EN learner plans the module differently than an LT one.
reviewFindings.direction: Retranslate hero subtext and outcomes from LT, keeping the depth/roles wording and the "you will apply context engineering to agents" transfer claim; align the stated duration with LT.

reviewFindings.citation: "Agent engineering"
reviewFindings.problem: The EN subtitle is a two-word category label where LT carries the slide's whole teaching frame ("Kontrolės režimas pagal pasekmę ir atšaukimą" — control mode by consequence and reversibility). Since all three EN bodies are also boilerplate (A1-01), the subtitle was the last place an EN learner could have picked up the consequence × reversibility idea, and it is gone.
reviewFindings.direction: Translate the LT subtitle; keep "consequence" and "reversibility" visible in EN since they are the two axes the lab is built on.

reviewFindings.citation: "Agent cycle and architecture"
reviewFindings.problem: The EN checkpoint's inner title is a verbatim copy of the previous slide's title, so in EN the learner sees the same heading twice in a row and cannot tell that slide 4 is a do-and-mark step rather than a repeat of slide 3. LT distinguishes them by phrasing the checkpoint as a completed action ("atlikau 1 agentinę užklausą"), and the EN subtitle also drops the step number that LT carries.
reviewFindings.direction: Translate the LT completion-phrased title and restore the step number in the EN subtitle so the checkpoint reads as a distinct, markable step.

reviewFindings.citation: "Be papildomų skaidrių (GitHub deep, testavimo/saugumo deep, žodynėlis)."
reviewFindings.problem: The short path is defined twice with two different contents. Here it drops three things (GitHub, testing/safety deep, glossary); the next slide's optional list adds a fourth, "santrauka" ("**Neprivaloma:** GitHub, gilesnė specifikacija, žodynėlis, santrauka."). A learner who picks the short path on slide 1 cannot tell whether the module summary is part of their path. "GitHub deep" and "testavimo/saugumo deep" also carry the internal word "deep" into learner copy.
reviewFindings.direction: Make one list authoritative and mirror it on both slides, using slide names in plain LT instead of "deep"; decide explicitly whether the summary is inside the short path.

reviewFindings.citation: "**MUST kelias:** agentų ciklas → 3A strategija → gylis ir rolės"
reviewFindings.problem: "MUST" is an untranslated English word in visible LT copy, and it is paired with a Lithuanian antonym ("**Neprivaloma:**"), so the two labels do not read as a pair. A non-technical learner has to infer that MUST is the opposite of Neprivaloma. The plain-language guide asks to avoid English shorthand in learner-visible text.
reviewFindings.direction: Use a Lithuanian pair (mandatory / optional) for the two labels so the contrast is obvious without knowing English.

reviewFindings.citation: "Diagrama žemiau – **penki ciklo žingsniai**."
reviewFindings.problem: The slide says five steps, but the subtitle right above it shows a six-item arrow chain: "Agentas → Planavimas → Įrankiai → Aplinka → Rezultatas → Grįžtamasis ryšys". A learner who counts gets six and doubts the text or the diagram. The SOT keeps feedback out of the numbered chain ("**Agentas → Planavimas → Įrankiai → Aplinka → Rezultatas** + grįžtamasis ryšys") and requires prose and copyable to match the five diagram steps; the live subtitle promotes feedback to a sixth sequential node. The copyable then numbers a third variant, starting from the task rather than from the agent.
reviewFindings.direction: Present feedback as a return arrow rather than a sixth chain item, and use the same five step names in subtitle, prose and copyable.

reviewFindings.citation: "Išsamiau, kada agentas, o kada paprastas promptas – su pavyzdžiais – skaidrėje"
reviewFindings.problem: A section titled "Kada rinktis agentą" answers nothing — it only points to a later slide. The learner has just been told the cycle and is primed for the choice, and instead hits a signpost. The target slide does exist, so nothing is broken, but a heading that raises the question and defers it entirely spends attention for no gain.
reviewFindings.direction: Either give one decision line here (the shortest possible rule of thumb) and then point onward, or fold the pointer into the neighbouring section instead of giving it its own heading.

reviewFindings.citation: "Kai reikia darbo eigos su triggeriu ir veiksmais"
reviewFindings.problem: A distractor uses "triggeriu" as if it were known vocabulary. In this module the term is introduced as "Paleidiklis (trigger)" on the workflow-concepts slide, which comes much later in the sequence. At slide 5 a non-technical learner is asked to reject an option they cannot parse, so the question tests vocabulary instead of the agent-vs-prompt judgment it intends to test.
reviewFindings.direction: Use the Lithuanian term (with the English in brackets on first appearance) or phrase the distractor without the term, e.g. via a concrete event that starts a flow.

reviewFindings.citation: "Agentinė užduotis turi kelių žingsnių logiką, įrankių naudojimą arba sprendimą, ar kartoti veiksmą."
reviewFindings.problem: None of the three explanations tells a learner who answered wrong where to go back. The SOT specifies a remediation route for this warm-up ("Jei klysti – grįžk į 10.2 ir 10.21"), and the surrounding content-block slides all end with an explicit fallback, so the quiz is the one place in this batch where a failed check leads nowhere.
reviewFindings.direction: Add a short back-pointer to the cycle slide and the checkpoint in the explanations (by slide name, not ID), at least for the two conceptual questions.

reviewFindings.citation: "Warm-up: cycle"
reviewFindings.problem: EN names this slide two ways: the title is "Quick check: agent cycle" while the short title (and therefore the previous slide's footer, "Next – slide 5: Warm-up: cycle") calls it "Warm-up: cycle". The learner is promised one slide and lands on a differently named one. LT is consistent ("Savitikra" in both), and "Warm-up" is closer to the internal slide-type name than to learner language.
reviewFindings.direction: Pick one EN name for this slide and use it in title, short title and the referring footer.

reviewFindings.citation: "**Automatizuoti (80 %)** – kiek: taisyklės be žmogaus kiekviename žingsnyje."
reviewFindings.problem: The label "kiek:" asks how much, and the text after it answers what the band is. The amount is already in the heading (80 %), so the label is both redundant and wrong for the sentence it introduces, in all three bands. It is a small snag on an otherwise exemplary slide, but it makes the first band read as a broken sentence. The SOT prescribes the same Kiek/Kodėl/Pvz. triplet, so the label set should be reconsidered there too.
reviewFindings.direction: Rename the first label to match what it actually answers (what the band is / what happens) and let the percentage in the heading carry the "how much"; keep the parallel three-line structure.

reviewFindings.citation: "Ar gali pasakyti, kurį **vieną įprotį** komanda turi sustiprinti prieš agentinį darbą?"
reviewFindings.problem: The slide asks the learner to choose across "trijose dimensijose" and to read which "dimensija" is weakest, then the gate switches to "įprotis" (habit). Two words for one thing on a three-block slide makes the learner check whether they missed a distinction. "Dimensija" is also the more abstract of the two for a business audience, and the three dimensions are never named in the slide text — only inside the lab.
reviewFindings.direction: Use one term throughout (the concrete one is the better learner word) and name the three areas in the body so the slide is readable before the lab is touched.

reviewFindings.citation: "Komandos pasirengimo agentiniam darbui lab'as"
reviewFindings.problem: The alternative text still uses "lab'as" — the apostrophe-loanword form that was removed elsewhere. Alt text is learner-facing for screen-reader users, so this is the one remaining place on the slide where an internal word reaches the learner. EN drifts the same way in the body ("The lab generates a team readiness profile") where LT says the profile appears below, giving screen-reader and EN users a component name instead of an outcome.
reviewFindings.direction: Describe what the visual is and what it produces in plain LT, without the loanword; align the EN body with LT's "you will get a profile below" framing.

reviewFindings.citation: "Ar atsakyme yra bent 2 žingsniai? Ar nurodyta, kokį įrankį DI naudojo arba kodėl jo nenaudojo?"
reviewFindings.problem: The copyable asks the model for a three-part answer ("Pateik atsakymą 3 žingsniais: ką darei, kokį įrankį naudojai, koks rezultatas"), and the check immediately above asks whether there are at least two steps. The learner is left holding two different numbers for the same output and cannot tell whether a two-part answer passes or fails their own gate.
reviewFindings.direction: Make the check count the same thing the prompt requests (either the three named answer parts, or process steps stated as a separate idea), so the gate is unambiguous.

reviewFindings.citation: "Nukopijuok šią taisyklę į darbo eigos aprašymą (skaidrė 10.64, 8 punktas)."
reviewFindings.problem: The one instruction that tells the learner where the generated rule goes is factually wrong and breaks a hard project convention at the same time. Slide 10.64 ("Minimalus darbo eigos aprašymas") is organized as parts A / B / C — there is no numbered "8 punktas"; the 8-block specification lives on a different slide (10.65) and its eighth block is the audit log, not human approval. A learner who follows the hint looks for a slot that does not exist, in the wrong document. On top of that, the curriculum ID `10.64` is exposed in learner-facing copy, where only slide names are allowed. The EN string repeats both errors: "Copy this rule into the workflow brief (slide 10.64, item 8)."
reviewFindings.direction: Point at the target by its learner-visible name and by the part that actually receives the rule (the human-decision part of the minimal workflow brief), and drop the numeric slide reference entirely. Keep LT and EN naming identical to that slide's own title in each locale.

reviewFindings.path: src/components/slides/shared/m10HumanControlContent.ts ; formatControlRuleArtefact → line 2 via conditionLine (condition is keyed to the scenario only, never to the chosen mode)
reviewFindings.citation: "Žmogaus peržiūra, kai tonas neaiškus, trūksta faktų arba atsakymas nėra standartinis FAQ."
reviewFindings.problem: The artifact's approval condition depends only on the scenario, so it can flatly contradict the mode printed one line above it. Choose "Atsakymas klientui" + "Rezultatų stebėsena" (a mode whose own description is "Be individualių atvejų peržiūros") and the copied rule reads "Kontrolės režimas: Rezultatų stebėsena" followed by "Patvirtinimo sąlyga / riba: Žmogaus peržiūra, kai tonas neaiškus…" — a per-case human review inside a mode that has no per-case review. The same collision happens for "Asmens duomenys ar mokėjimas" + "Patikra po veiksmo", where the condition insists on approval *before* the action. This is the artifact the learner pastes into their brief and shows a colleague, so the incoherence travels.
reviewFindings.direction: Make the condition line depend on scenario *and* mode: for weak modes it should state the sampling or monitoring trigger and what is explicitly not gated, or the artifact should state that the selected mode does not satisfy the scenario's condition. Same shape in both locales.

reviewFindings.path: src/components/slides/shared/m10DepthRolesContent.ts ; getDepthRolesUiLabels (en) → teamRolesNote, routerToggle; formatDepthRolesArtefact (en) router line
reviewFindings.citation: "Team needs three roles: coordinator, specialist, evaluator. Router only if you need triage before the coordinator."
reviewFindings.problem: The EN lab still explains the router as "triage", while its own EN slide says the router is for requests that "must first be sorted by type", and the LT lab says exactly that ("išskirstyti pagal tipą"). So the EN learner meets a medical/support loanword where the surrounding slide deliberately avoids it, and the mismatch repeats three times, including inside the copied artifact ("– how they triage before the coordinator (+ input / output)"). The word also carries no gloss, so the least confident EN reader gets the least help exactly at the optional-role decision.
reviewFindings.direction: Bring the three EN strings onto the slide's wording (sorting requests by type before the coordinator) so the toggle, the note and the artifact line all describe the same rule, and mirror the LT phrasing that already passed review.

reviewFindings.citation: "Rule: start from Agent – pick Team or Flow only when one agent is not enough or you need a trigger."
reviewFindings.problem: Only the LT side of this lab was rewritten. LT now teaches two distinct signals — Team when you need several roles, Flow when an event starts actions automatically — and matches the slide sentence word for word. EN still collapses both into "one agent is not enough or you need a trigger", and the EN Flow option is labelled "Trigger → actions (automation)" where LT says the event starts the actions. An EN learner therefore gets a vaguer rule than the LT learner and than the EN slide above the lab, which is the exact failure mode the "same semantics in both locales" rule exists to prevent.
reviewFindings.direction: Port the LT rule and the LT Flow description into EN so both locales name the two signals separately, and keep the Flow description behavioral (an event starts the actions) rather than a bare noun arrow.

reviewFindings.citation: "e.g. email · research · RFP · form → CRM"
reviewFindings.problem: The hint whose whole job is to help a non-technical reader pick a process from their own work is written in two unglossed acronyms. LT solved this by replacing them with plain nouns ("sutartis", "klientų sistema"); EN kept the procurement and sales-tooling shorthand. A business reader outside sales or bid management has to decode "RFP" before they can even start the lab.
reviewFindings.direction: Replace both acronyms in EN with the same kind of plain examples LT uses (a contract or proposal; a customer system), or gloss them on first use in the lab.

reviewFindings.citation: "Use it when DI helps prepare the answer, but a person keeps accountability."
reviewFindings.problem: A Lithuanian term is hardcoded inside an English learner string. "DI" is the LT abbreviation for AI; in the EN interface it reads as an unexplained two-letter code, and it violates the locale rule that LT uses DI while EN uses AI. This is the walkthrough body for the middle 3A band, i.e. the sentence that teaches where human accountability sits, so the confusion lands on the most important idea of the slide.
reviewFindings.direction: Use the EN term for the technology in every EN string of this file, and check the other two band bodies in the same pass.

reviewFindings.citation: "Trys praktikos: Automatizuoti, Asistuoti, Autonomizuoti — žmogaus vartai paryškinti chip eigoje"
reviewFindings.problem: The screen-reader description of the diagram is written in build vocabulary, not learner vocabulary. "Chip" is the internal name for the small step pill; a learner using assistive technology hears that the human gate is highlighted "chip eigoje", which describes an implementation detail they cannot see and never had defined. EN has the same problem ("human gate highlighted on the chip flow"). Learners who rely on the aria text are the ones who most need the plain description of the three flows.
reviewFindings.direction: Describe what the diagram shows in learner words in both locales — three flows of steps with the point where a human approves highlighted — and drop the component vocabulary from the aria strings.

reviewFindings.citation: "title: 'Three mandatory labs (3A)',"
reviewFindings.problem: The EN diagram calls the three M12 exercises "labs" while its own EN slide, its footer and its step navigation call them "practices" — and the LT side has already been aligned on "praktikos". The learner therefore has to guess whether "Lab 1" and "Practice 1" are the same thing before choosing which one to open next, which is precisely the action this slide asks for. The word "mandatory" also appears nowhere on the slide.
reviewFindings.direction: Use the slide's noun ("practices") consistently across title, region, nav and step aria in EN, and keep the mandatory/optional status out of the diagram heading since the slide already frames it.

reviewFindings.citation: "logs: ['Logs', 'steps, errors, feedback'],"
reviewFindings.problem: The EN diagram labels three boxes with names the EN slide never uses. The slide subtitle promises "Rules, skills, action history, check and lessons" and its glossary-style section defines "**Action history**" and "**Check**"; the diagram shows "Logs" and "Evaluation", and calls the last box "Learning update" where the slide says "Update". LT was renamed to "Veiksmų istorija" / "Patikra" and matches its slide exactly, so this is a one-sided update. The learner is asked to click each box and read the explanation, so mismatched names break the mapping between the text and the picture.
reviewFindings.direction: Rename the EN nodes to the slide's own terms (action history, check, update) and keep the EN step bodies using the same nouns.

reviewFindings.citation: "Veiksmų istorija fiksuoja žingsnius, klaidas ir pastabas. Be logų nėra iš ko mokytis kitam bandymui."
reviewFindings.problem: One sentence uses both the plain LT term and the loanword for the same thing. The node label and the slide were deliberately moved to "veiksmų istorija"; the very next clause reverts to "logų", so the learner cannot tell whether these are one concept or two, and the de-jargonizing work done on the label is undone in the body the learner reads after clicking it.
reviewFindings.direction: Keep one LT name for this box throughout the step body, matching the node label and the slide.

reviewFindings.citation: "agents: ['Agentai', 'tyrėjas, rašytojas, QA'],"
reviewFindings.problem: The three specialists are named "tyrėjas, rašytojas, QA" here, but the immediately preceding orchestration slide teaches them as Tyrėjas, Rašytojas and Tikrintojas, and the module spends a whole slide on the Tikrintojas-versus-Vertintojas distinction. Swapping the third role for an unglossed English acronym both loses that distinction and introduces a term with no definition anywhere in the learner path (EN has the same "QA").
reviewFindings.direction: Reuse the role names established on the orchestration slide in both locales so the learning loop shows the same three specialists the learner just met.

reviewFindings.citation: "state: ['Būsena', 'atmintis / changelog'],"
reviewFindings.problem: A core box in the walkthrough is subtitled with a bare English developer word, and the step body repeats it ("Būsena (atmintis / changelog) saugo kontekstą ir kas jau bandyta."). The parentheses look like a gloss but hold a second English word, so a non-technical LT reader gets no plain explanation of what the state actually keeps. The slide itself says only "planą, būseną ir bandymus", so the diagram is introducing terminology the slide never asked for.
reviewFindings.direction: Describe what the box holds in plain LT (what has already been tried, what context carries over) and keep the loanword out, or gloss it properly on first mention if it must stay.

reviewFindings.citation: "Sistema gauna RFP užduotį: paruošti trumpą santrauką (5 punktai)"
reviewFindings.problem: The entire six-step walkthrough is built on an unglossed procurement acronym, repeated in the specialists step ("Tyrėjas per įrankius ieško šaltinių RFP punktams"). A learner in operations, HR or finance has to reverse-engineer the scenario before they can follow the router-versus-orchestrator lesson, which is the actual teaching point. The slide shares the gap, so this needs a coordinated fix rather than a silent divergence.
reviewFindings.direction: Either gloss the term once at the input step in both locales, or restate the scenario with a plain business artifact (a proposal or tender summary with mandatory sources) and align the slide wording in the same pass.

reviewFindings.citation: "steps: ['Stabdyti', 'Fiksuoti', 'Apimtis', 'Pranešti', 'Ištaisyti'],"
reviewFindings.problem: The five incident steps are named differently in the diagram than in the slide that describes them. The slide lists "sustabdyti → fiksuoti → įvertinti → pranešti → ištaisyti" and repeats that list in two later M12 slides, while the diagram's third step is the noun "Apimtis" — a different idea (scope) presented in a different part of speech from its four sibling verbs. EN drifts on two of five ("Log" and "Scope" against the slide's "record" and "assess"). A learner copying the playbook into their own incident rule cannot tell which five words are canonical.
reviewFindings.direction: Adopt one canonical set of five step names per locale, matching the slide and the M12 references, and keep all five in the same grammatical form.

reviewFindings.citation: "title: 'Verslo kelių agentų srautas',"
reviewFindings.problem: The diagram heading renames its own slide — the slide is "Verslo kelių agentų schema" / "Business multi-agent schema" — and it picks the one word the module has already reserved for something else. In the depth taxonomy the learner just completed, "Srautas" is depth level L3, defined as an event automatically starting actions; this picture is a Team (L2) with a coordinator and specialists, no trigger anywhere. Calling it a "srautas" teaches the learner that the two levels are the same thing.
reviewFindings.direction: Match the slide's noun in both locales ("schema") in the title and the aria description, and keep "Srautas / Flow" reserved for the L3 depth level.

reviewFindings.citation: "Šis režimas per silpnai kontroliuoja riziką. Rekomenduojama:"
reviewFindings.problem: Three of the four mismatch messages teach the mechanism — spot checks only find the error after the action, monitoring alone is too weak for this consequence — but this one only restates the verdict. It is the message a learner sees when they pick exception review for the sensitive-data / payment scenario, i.e. the single most instructive near-miss in the lab: the choice is defensible for most work and wrong here specifically because the consequence is critical and the action cannot be reversed. The copy never says that, so the learner is corrected without learning the rule. EN has the same gap ("This mode under-controls the risk. Recommended:").
reviewFindings.direction: Name the two factors that force the stronger gate (critical consequence, hard to reverse) so the feedback teaches the same decision rule the risk strip visualizes; keep it one sentence, both locales.

reviewFindings.citation: "Pvz.: tyrimo agentas → kokybės kontrolė → eskalacija, jei neaišku."
reviewFindings.problem: The band walkthrough gives a different example from the slide text a few centimetres above it, which says "atsiliepimai → nuotaika → eskalacija žmogui" (EN: "feedback → sentiment → escalate to a human"). The same reviews-and-sentiment example is also the one carried forward into the M12 templates, so the diagram's research-agent example is the odd one out and quietly competes with the example the learner is later asked to reuse.
reviewFindings.direction: Reuse the slide's example for this band in both locales, or make the diagram example explicitly a second case rather than a substitute.

reviewFindings.citation: "Fiksuok run_id, laiką, žingsnį, sprendimą ir rezultatą, kad komanda vėliau galėtų audituoti eigą."
reviewFindings.problem: A raw code identifier stands where the LT slide uses a plain phrase ("vykdymo ID"). A business learner writing their own audit line copies a field name from a system they may not have, instead of the idea that each run needs its own identifier.
reviewFindings.direction: Use the slide's plain LT wording for the identifier and keep the rest of the field list as is.

reviewFindings.citation: "rankinis mygtukas, webhook ar kitas aiškus signalas."
reviewFindings.problem: The same file glosses this word properly in the trigger-flow diagram ("Internetinis pranešimas (webhook) = paleidiklio tipas") and the glossary defines it as "internetinis pranešimas", but the specification body drops the bare loanword into a list of otherwise plain LT items, so the learner meets an unexplained term in the one place they are listing their own starting signal.
reviewFindings.direction: Use the glossed LT form here as well, matching the trigger-flow diagram and the glossary entry.

reviewFindings.problem: The visible block chip is a bare acronym while the screen-reader description of the same block says "Išvestis, paslaugos lygis, Klaidos ir Auditas". Sighted and assistive-technology learners are shown two different names for block six, and only one of them is plain LT. The slide that describes these blocks glosses it as "Paslaugos lygis (SLA)", so the plain form already exists.
reviewFindings.direction: Make the visible chip and the aria description agree, using the slide's glossed LT form.

reviewFindings.citation: "condition: 'Self-host / data on-prem'"
reviewFindings.problem: This branch condition is the only one in the tree written in infrastructure shorthand, and its LT counterpart is fully plain ("Savas serveris / duomenys pas mus"). The decision tree exists so a non-technical reader can pick a platform; "on-prem" makes the branch that is actually about data staying in-house the hardest one to read.
reviewFindings.direction: Restate the EN condition in the same plain terms as LT (own server, data stays with us).

reviewFindings.citation: "updateRules: 'atnaujina sistemą',"
reviewFindings.problem: Three separately named label slots all carry the identical string, in both locales. Whatever the two per-target labels were meant to say (updates the rules, updates the skills), that copy was never written, so the diagram can only ever say the generic version and the interface promises a distinction the copy does not deliver.
reviewFindings.direction: Either write the two specific labels, or retire the unused keys so the copy surface matches what is actually taught.

reviewFindings.citation: "orchestrator: ['Koordinatorius', 'planuoja, skirsto'],"
reviewFindings.problem: The plan-and-assign box is "Koordinatorius" here and "Orkestratorius" one slide earlier ("orchestrator: ['Orkestratorius', 'planas + bandymai'],"), and the glossary defines only the first — "Kelių agentų rolė, kuri suskaido užduotį, paskiria specialistus ir sujungia jų rezultatus." — with no entry for the second. Since the orchestration slide spends its whole "Trys skirtumai" section separating router from orchestrator, meeting the same function under a second, glossary-less name invites the learner to treat them as different things.
reviewFindings.direction: Decide one learner-facing name per function across M10 and M12, keep the other as a bilingual first mention if it must appear, and hand the glossary gap to DATA.

reviewFindings.citation: "gapLabel: 'Pagrindinis tarpas',"
reviewFindings.problem: This label names the concept "tarpas" (a physical space) where the rest of M10 uses "spraga" for the same idea — the learning-loop diagram's check box is subtitled "kriterijai, spragos". The readiness snapshot's single most important output is this line, so the term that carries it should be the one the module uses elsewhere.
reviewFindings.direction: Align the LT label with the module's existing term for a gap, and check the profile artifact line that echoes it.

reviewFindings.citation: "matrixHeading: 'Kur tu esi rizikoje',"
reviewFindings.problem: The two locales head the same risk strip with different subjects: LT addresses the learner ("where you are"), EN describes the scenario ("Where this sits on risk"). The strip plots the three business scenarios, not the learner, so the LT heading also mislabels what the reader is looking at.
reviewFindings.direction: Use one meaning in both locales — where the selected scenario sits on consequence and reversibility — keeping the LT tu-form elsewhere in the lab.

reviewFindings.citation: "The every-case gate blocked a bad draft. No customer-facing action left the system."
reviewFindings.problem: The EN error-case result invents a name for the mode instead of quoting it. The mode is labelled "Approve every case"; LT quotes its own label verbatim („Visada tvirtina žmogus" vartai). A learner comparing the outcome panel with the option they just selected has to infer that "the every-case gate" is that option.
reviewFindings.direction: Quote the mode label in the EN outcome text the way LT does, so the feedback names the choice the learner made.

reviewFindings.citation: "Paruošti standartinį FAQ atsakymą prieš siuntimą ar vietoj jo."
reviewFindings.problem: An unglossed acronym sits in the first scenario every learner selects, and it reappears inside the copied artifact's approval condition. It is a mild case — the term is common — but the LT interface has a plain equivalent and the acronym is doing no work here beyond shorthand.
reviewFindings.direction: Use a plain phrase for a standard, frequently-asked-question answer in the LT strings, and keep the EN wording parallel.

reviewFindings.citation: "title: 'Agent orchestration walkthrough',"
reviewFindings.problem: The EN diagram heading and the EN slide title disagree — the slide is "Agent orchestration simulation", and the LT pair matches ("Agentų orkestravimo simuliacija" on both sides). Two headings for one picture is a small but avoidable friction, and it is the kind of drift that appears when only one locale is edited.
reviewFindings.direction: Match the EN diagram title to the EN slide title, or align both on one noun in the same pass.

reviewFindings.citation: "darbas grįžta koordinatoriui (punktyrinė feedback rodyklė), o ne į išvestį."
reviewFindings.problem: A bare English word sits in the middle of an otherwise plain LT sentence, where the project's own LT term is "grįžtamasis ryšys" (used as such on the agent-cycle slide). The clause is describing the one arrow the learner must notice — the return path that keeps failed work out of the output — so the loanword lands on the load-bearing detail.
reviewFindings.direction: Describe the arrow in plain LT (the dashed return arrow back to the coordinator) using the module's established term.

reviewFindings.citation: "steps: ['Email', 'LLM', 'Approve', 'Send'],"
reviewFindings.problem: The same step box is "DI" in LT and "LLM" in EN, so the two locales name different things at the point where the learner is asked which step needs a human. The EN acronym is also unglossed on this slide. The slide's own pre-copy check repeats the divergence, so this needs coordinating with the JSON owner rather than fixing in one place.
reviewFindings.direction: Pick one concept name per locale for that box — the technology the learner has been taught, glossed if an acronym stays — and align the slide's check question with it.

reviewFindings.citation: "enlargeLabel: 'Trys praktikos (3A)',"
reviewFindings.problem: The diagram heading says "Trys privalomos praktikos (3A)" while the enlarge label of the same diagram says "Trys praktikos (3A)"; the slide title and shortTitle use the shorter form and never call them mandatory. One of the two strings was updated and the other was not, so the learner sees the requirement wording only in one place.
reviewFindings.direction: Use one LT name for this diagram in both strings, matching the slide, and let the mandatory/optional framing live in the slide copy.

reviewFindings.citation: "Use this step to design, test and improve an AI agent workflow with clear tools, limits and human approval"
reviewFindings.problem: All three EN body fields carry the same generic filler sentence. LT teaches something different in each: the intro says the depth is already chosen and only inputs/outputs/handoff rule are needed; `sections[0]` asks two check questions (when does the specialist hand off, does the evaluator have a done criterion); `sections[1]` gives the fallback (drop to one agent, one tool, one result). The EN learner gets no instruction, no gate and no fallback — the checkpoint cannot be completed. The same filler sentence occurs 12× in `src/data/modules-en-m10-m12.json`, so this is unfinished authoring, not a translation choice.
reviewFindings.direction: Translate the three LT fields as three distinct texts; keep the LT split of intro / check questions / fallback. Treat the other 11 occurrences of the filler as the same defect class in the remaining M10–12 path-steps.

reviewFindings.citation: "Role: agent assistant. Task: review the process, use tools only when needed, return a clear result"
reviewFindings.problem: The EN copyable is a generic single-agent role prompt, not a translation of the LT one. LT hands the learner the checkpoint artifact: process + level, then input / output / handoff rule for coordinator, specialist and evaluator. EN produces a different artifact that does not answer the slide's own check questions and does not carry the three roles forward to the path's next step. The EN learner leaves the checkpoint with nothing reusable.
reviewFindings.direction: Replace with a real translation of the LT template, preserving the `[APRAŠYK]`-equivalent placeholder, the level marker and the three role lines with input / output / handoff rule.

reviewFindings.citation: "AI agent workflow step."
reviewFindings.problem: The EN glossary reward is the same placeholder string three times, where LT unlocks three real terms (`Koordinatorius`, `Vertintojas`, `Maršrutizatorius`). The path-step reward shown to the EN learner is meaningless text, and the three role terms the slide is built around never enter the EN glossary.
reviewFindings.direction: Map the three LT terms to their EN glossary entries (coordinator / evaluator / router) so the unlock matches the roles taught on 10.45 and 10.451.

reviewFindings.citation: "AI agent step"
reviewFindings.problem: LT `content.title` is a learner achievement statement in the first person — "Rolės – apibrėžiau įvestis ir išvestis" — which is what makes a path step feel completed. EN replaces it with a flat label that names neither roles nor inputs/outputs. The same flattening hits `subtitle`: LT "Agentų inžinerijos kelias – žingsnis 2" vs EN "Agent engineering path step" loses the step index, so the EN learner cannot see where they are in a 3-step path.
reviewFindings.direction: Restore the first-person achievement framing in EN and re-add the step number to the subtitle, matching the LT pattern used across the path.

reviewFindings.citation: "kelių agentų rolės – skaidrėje **DI agentų tipai ir rolės**."
reviewFindings.problem: Three learner-facing places point to a slide called "DI agentų tipai ir rolės", but the slide that actually follows is titled "Pasirink agento gylį ir roles". 10.3 `content.footer` repeats the dead name ("Toliau – skaidrė 10: DI agentų tipai ir rolės") and 10.451 `content.body` repeats it again ("Lygį jau pasirinkai skaidrėje „DI agentų tipai ir rolės“."). EN is inconsistent in a second way: the 10.3 footer already uses the new name ("Next – slide 10: Agent depth and roles") while the EN body still says "on **AI agent types and roles**". A learner who wants to go back cannot find the slide by the name they were given. [SOT-KONFLIKTAS] SOT §3b2 heading: "## 3b2. DI agentų tipai ir rolės (skaidrė 10.45)" vs live `title`: "Pasirink agento gylį ir roles".
reviewFindings.direction: Pick one learner-facing name for 10.45 and propagate it to all three cross-references in both languages; update the SOT §3b2 heading in the same pass so the next author does not reintroduce the old name.

reviewFindings.path: content.body; also content.sections[0].copyable, content.sections[1].body, and 10.481 content.recap.items[0]
reviewFindings.citation: "trims rolėms (jei L2). Jei likai L1 – pažymėk žingsnį ir eik toliau."
reviewFindings.problem: The whole checkpoint branches on bare codes. `content.body` uses "jei L2" and "Jei likai L1", the copyable says "(lygis jau: L2)", the fallback says "Sumažink iki L1", and the recap on 10.481 says "Gylis L0–L3 – kada pakanka vieno agento, kada reikia kelių." The codes are only ever paired with their names inside the 10.45 lab badges; nothing on 10.451 or 10.481 re-states them. A non-technical learner who skipped or half-read the lab cannot tell whether they are "L1" or "L2" and therefore cannot decide which branch of the checkpoint applies to them.
reviewFindings.direction: Lead with the name and keep the code as a parenthetical on first mention per slide (name-first, code-second — the pattern the SOT §3b2 table already prescribes: "pirminė kalba = vardas; L\* = kodas").

reviewFindings.citation: "**Ne:** rezultatas be kokybės rizikos – pakanka L1."
reviewFindings.problem: This is the only place in 10.48 where a depth code appears, and LT gives it bare. EN glosses it in the same field — "**No:** low quality risk – Agent (L1) is enough." — so the EN learner sees the name and the LT learner does not. The hint is a decision rule at the moment of choosing a pattern, so an unreadable "L1" costs the learner the comparison.
reviewFindings.direction: Mirror the EN gloss in LT (name + code) so the choice bar hint is self-sufficient.

reviewFindings.citation: "Pereik visus 6 žingsnius."
reviewFindings.problem: Verified — the slide has five sections (Trumpai, Simuliacija, Daryk dabar, Patikra, Trys skirtumai) and no `copyable` anywhere. The diagram and its six step explanations are the strongest teaching asset in the batch, but the only action asked for is walking the steps and the only output is two recall answers in the learner's head. Nothing leaves the slide: no orchestration plan, no retry rule, no gate criteria the learner could reuse on their own process. Against GOLDEN §3.2 the "Kopijuojamas promptas" section is simply missing, and 10.482 sits between two slides (10.48, 10.49) that both hand over an artifact.
reviewFindings.direction: Add one small copyable that converts the walkthrough into the learner's own case — the plan order, what state to keep, and the retry rule (what gets rerun vs escalated). Keep it short; the value is the retry/escalation decision, not length.

reviewFindings.citation: "Maršrutizatorius ≠ orkestratorius; Tikrintojas ≠ Vertintojas; tikslinis retry"
reviewFindings.problem: "retry" stays untranslated in LT in the slide subtitle, in Trumpai ("klaida → **tikslinis** retry, ne visas paleidimas iš naujo.") and in the 10.481 recap ("orkestratorius = KAIP (planas ir retry)."). Worse, the same concept gets three names inside one slide: the collapsible says "orkestratorius valdo planą, būseną ir bandymus.", the diagram edge and step title say "KARTOTI", and the headline copy says "retry". The learner has to work out that bandymai = KARTOTI = retry before they can answer the Patikra question, which is exactly the distinction this slide exists to teach.
