reviewFindings.problem: One module earlier the learner was drilled on a named distinction: router = WHERE, **orchestrator** = HOW. Here the same chain appears with the router intact but the orchestrator silently replaced by **koordinatorius**, with no bridging sentence. In M10 "koordinatorius" was one of five workflow *patterns*, not the managing role, so the learner cannot tell whether the coordinator is the orchestrator under a new name, a different role, or a demotion. The `whyBenefit` does point back to the M10 slide by name, which makes the unexplained term swap more jarring, not less. The reported overlap with `10.482` is otherwise handled honestly — `whyBenefit` states this slide is only the practice map and the handoff rule.
reviewFindings.direction: Add one sentence tying the terms together (the coordinator is the orchestrator role in this business-level map) or use the M10 term. Same decision must cover the diagram labels in `m12MultiAgentSchemaContent.ts` and the checkpoint chain on `120.55`.

reviewFindings.problem: Parity is broken in the direction that hurts the primary language. EN gives a worked example of the handoff rule *and* a consequence sentence ("Without handoff multi-agent becomes chaotic"); LT gives only an abstract three-part enumeration. Since the very next thing the LT learner must do is write one handoff rule, LT is missing the model answer that EN readers get, and also the motivation for why the rule matters.
reviewFindings.direction: Bring the concrete example and the "why it matters" sentence into LT (LT is the source of truth), then re-derive EN from it so the two match.

reviewFindings.problem: Within one slide the same concept is called `vaidmuo` (heading, `sections[2].body`) and `rolė` (Patikra, and `[ROLĖ A]` / `[ROLĖ B]` in the copyable). A learner filling in the template has to guess that "kita rolė" and "kitas vaidmuo" are the same slot. Related naming drift: the diagram inside this slide is titled `Verslo kelių agentų srautas` (`src/components/slides/shared/m12MultiAgentSchemaContent.ts`) while the slide, its section heading and its `shortTitle` all say *schema* — two names for one object.
reviewFindings.direction: Fix one LT term for the concept across headings, body, copyable placeholders and Patikra, and align the diagram title with the slide title (or vice versa).

reviewFindings.problem: The intro sets the completion contract (3 required practices, `requiredSlideIds: [121, 122, 123]`, `~60–90 min visos 3 praktikos`) but never says that all three are built on external automation platforms, nor that a no-account fallback exists. The only hint is indirect and by omission: one path is "be papildomų įrankių", another assumes "jei jau turi aiškų procesą ir įrankį". A learner without a Zapier/Make account therefore picks a path unable to judge whether they can finish, and cannot see that `121`/`122` explicitly allow a platform-ready document instead — the very reassurance that would keep them going. The SOT's `Projekto apžvalga` (§8.1), which names the three practice flows, is also not reflected anywhere on this slide.
reviewFindings.direction: Add one honest line to the intro naming the tool expectation for practices 1–3 **and** the document fallback for learners without an account, plus a compact one-line overview of the three flows. Do not soften the 3-required-practices rule; the problem is disclosure, not scope.

reviewFindings.citation: `In the Augment band (Email → LLM → Approve → Send) – which point needs a human?`
reviewFindings.problem: LT names the step `DI`; EN names it `LLM` — a technical term the training never introduces to a business learner, and one that contradicts the EN explanation two lines below, which calls the same actor `AI`. Convention for EN copy is `AI`. The same `LLM` label is in the EN diagram row (`m12ThreeLabsContent.ts`), so the question, the diagram and the explanation currently use two different names for one node in the flow the learner is being quizzed on.
reviewFindings.direction: Standardize on `AI` in EN across the question, the diagram row and the explanation, keeping `DI` in LT.

reviewFindings.citation: `Use it when DI helps prepare the answer, but a person keeps accountability.`
reviewFindings.problem: The EN lab explanation uses the Lithuanian abbreviation `DI`, which is untranslated and meaningless to an English learner — and it appears in the step explanation that opens when they click the Augment row, i.e. the payoff of the interaction. It also contradicts the EN slide copy, which says `AI` (`Augment = AI drafts…`).
reviewFindings.direction: Replace `DI` with `AI` in the EN branch of this file and check the other EN branches in the M12 diagram content modules for the same leak.

reviewFindings.problem: The checkpoint's "mini trial" asks for four things — split the task, write a separate specialist prompt for each part, specify the handoff format, add a human-approval point. That is the deliverable of slide `124.5` (the quick start) produced one slide earlier, so the learner either does the work twice or arrives at `124.5` with nothing new to do, and the "quick start" loses its purpose. The "(1 min)" label also mis-sets expectations for a four-part prompt that produces two sub-prompts plus a handoff format; a learner who takes ten minutes concludes they are slow.
reviewFindings.direction: Narrow the checkpoint to a genuine verification of the schema (e.g. name the roles and the gate for your own topic in one line) and let `124.5` own the prompt chain, or drop the trial and keep only the recall check; then re-time the label honestly.

reviewFindings.citation: `žmogaus vartai paryškinti chip eigoje`
reviewFindings.problem: The implementation term `chip` is still present in learner-facing Lithuanian text — the diagram's aria description, i.e. the only description a screen-reader user gets of this comparison. `chip` is not a Lithuanian word and names a UI widget the learner has no reason to know, and the LT hint right below already describes the same thing without it (`Paspausk praktikos eilutę – kur yra žmogaus vartai`).
reviewFindings.direction: Describe what the learner perceives (the highlighted step in the flow) instead of the widget, matching the wording already used in the LT hint and in the slide's `Palyginimas` body.

reviewFindings.citation: `punktyrinė feedback rodyklė`
reviewFindings.problem: An English loanword sits in the LT explanation of the evaluator step — the one place that explains the return loop, the hardest idea in the schema. Lithuanian has a settled term here, and the same file uses `grąžinimas` / `grąžina` elsewhere, so the loanword is also internally inconsistent.
reviewFindings.direction: Use the Lithuanian term already used in this file (return / return arrow) and keep the "dashed arrow" visual cue.

reviewFindings.problem: The band names and the numbers themselves match module 10 exactly (`Automatizuoti 80 % / Asistuoti 15 % / Autonomizuoti 5 %`) — no factual error. The risk is semantic: in M10 the percentages describe how a *portfolio of processes* should be distributed, while here they are attached to three practices that are equally required and equally weighted (one artifact each). A learner can reasonably read "praktika 1 (80 %)" as "practice 1 is most of the project" and treat practices 2 and 3 as marginal — the opposite of the completion rule.
reviewFindings.direction: Keep the numbers (they are the anchor to M10) but add a half-sentence restating that the percentages describe how many of *your processes* belong in each band, not how much of module 12 each practice is worth. Same applies to the `(80 %)` / `(15 %)` / `(5 %)` suffixes in the practice titles.

reviewFindings.citation: "nuoroda į incidentų planą (5 žingsniai) – skaidrė **Minimalus eigos aprašymas**."
reviewFindings.problem: `123` is one of the three practices that gate module completion, and one of its four required artifacts is a link to an incident playbook. That playbook is taught only on `10.65`, which is marked optional. A learner who took the mandatory path has never seen the five steps, so they hit a required deliverable for a concept they were never taught. The SOT confirms the placement rather than contradicting it: §11 MUST table says "optional 10.65 – PII, access, incident", so the defect is a curriculum-level dependency, not a typo.
reviewFindings.direction: either make the incident playbook available on the mandatory path (a compact five-step block inside `123` itself or promoted into `10.64`), or downgrade the artifact on `123` from "required link" to an explicitly optional deepening with a one-line inline definition of the five steps so the mandatory deliverable stays self-contained.

reviewFindings.citation: "5 žingsniai: sustabdyti, fiksuoti, įvertinti, pranešti, ištaisyti – skaidrė **Minimalus eigos aprašymas**."
reviewFindings.problem: the pointer is wrong. `Minimalus eigos aprašymas` (`10.64`) contains only Flow / Three tests / Human decision; it has no incident playbook at all (a search for "incident" in `10.64` returns nothing). The same wrong pointer is repeated three times on this slide — `scenario.expectedFormat`, `practicalTask.template` ("žr. **Minimalus eigos aprašymas**") and this step. A learner who follows the reference lands on a slide that does not contain the thing they were sent to fetch, and concludes either that they misread the task or that the five steps are the `10.64` template.
reviewFindings.direction: point at the slide that actually holds the playbook (`Darbo eigos testavimas ir saugumas`) in all three places, and resolve A8-01 first — pointing at an optional slide is still a dependency defect, so the fix for the reference and the fix for the dependency have to land together.

reviewFindings.citation: "\"taskFrame\": \"Task\""
reviewFindings.problem: the type is `taskFrame?: { task: string; doneWhen: string }` and the renderer prints `taskFrame.task` plus a "Done when:" line from `taskFrame.doneWhen`. A bare string is truthy, so on all three mandatory EN practices the task frame renders as an empty bordered box with the labels "Task:" and "Done when:" and no text after either. The EN learner therefore sees a visually prominent, blank acceptance-criteria block on precisely the three slides that decide whether they finish the module. LT has no `taskFrame` on these slides at all, so LT shows nothing — no broken box, but also no "done when" statement anywhere.
reviewFindings.direction: either author a real `{ task, doneWhen }` pair on both languages, derived from the existing `scenario.expectedFormat` artifact list (which already is the de facto completion test), or drop the field from EN. Do not leave one language with a rendered empty frame.

reviewFindings.citation: "Human-in-the-loop: before sending human approves or edits."
reviewFindings.problem: LT teaches a four-part control rule — mode (exception review), condition, rejection/escalation, audit trail — matching the `10.26` model. EN replaces the whole rule with a single clause saying a human approves before sending. The two versions teach opposite operating models: LT says review exceptions only, EN says approve everything. `practicalTask.explanation` repeats the split ("Išimčių peržiūra sumažina riziką, bet neapkrauna žmogaus kiekvienu standartiniu atveju." versus "Human approval reduces risk of wrong automatic send."). The EN learner leaves practice 2 with an artifact that has no escalation path and no audit line, so the artifact does not satisfy the SOT §8.2c requirement that this practice use the `10.26` control rule.
reviewFindings.direction: bring the EN template to LT parity (mode, condition, rejection/escalation, audit), and align `explanation` with exception review rather than blanket approval. This is a translation regression, not an intentional EN simplification.

reviewFindings.citation: "Artifacts: workflow diagram (1 p.), field mapping, min. 2 test cases, logs/screenshots."
reviewFindings.problem: EN carries the scenario twice, and the two copies do not agree on what counts as done. The live `scenario.expectedFormat` accepts a platform-ready document instead of a built automation and accepts "document excerpts" instead of logs; the duplicate in `content` drops both concessions and demands a diagram plus logs/screenshots — evidence only obtainable inside a Zapier or Make account. This is the single content consequence of the structural duplication: the account-free path that LT and the live EN scenario both guarantee is contradicted by the second copy on the same slide.
reviewFindings.direction: delete the duplicate scenario fields from the EN overlay so the slide has one source of truth for acceptance criteria; if a short lead-in is wanted, derive it from `scenario.expectedFormat` rather than restating a stricter artifact list.

reviewFindings.citation: "Artifacts: workflow diagram, summary prompt template, approval step description, 1–2 test cases."
reviewFindings.problem: same duplication defect as A8-05, with a second divergence: the duplicate asks for an "approval step description" while the live scenario asks for an "approval rule". Those are different deliverables — a description of a step versus the mode/condition/escalation/audit rule LT requires — and the duplicate also removes the document fallback for learners without an AI module. The learner sees two different artifact checklists on one slide and cannot tell which one is graded.
reviewFindings.direction: same as A8-05 — remove the duplicate block; keep "approval rule" as the single artifact name so EN matches LT and the `10.26` vocabulary.

reviewFindings.citation: "Užbaigei Agentų kelio projektą: kelių agentų startą tik su promptais arba pilną 3 praktikų kelią."
reviewFindings.problem: [SOT-KONFLIKTAS] The SOT states "**Privalomas progresas:** skaičiuojamos tik 3 praktikos `121`, `122`, `123`". Both language versions of the closing slide tell the learner something weaker. LT frames the prompt-only quick start as an alternative that completes the project; EN goes further and congratulates a learner for "at least one of 3 required practices". The final slide of the corporate track therefore certifies completion on criteria the product does not use, and the same false claim is repeated inside `content.reflectionPrompt` where the learner pastes it into an AI. Anyone who stops after `124.5` is told they are done.
reviewFindings.direction: state the actual completion rule once, in both languages — three practices are required, `124.5` and `124` are extras — and mirror it in the reflection prompt INPUT line so the copyable artifact does not carry the wrong claim into the learner's AI chat.

reviewFindings.citation: "\"ownWorkTemplate\": \"AI agent workflow step.\""
reviewFindings.problem: five consecutive EN fields — `abilityBefore`, `abilityAfter`, `ownWorkLabel`, `ownWorkPlaceholder`, `ownWorkTemplate` — all contain the same placeholder sentence "AI agent workflow step." LT has real content in each: a before/after ability pair, a field label, an example, and a working META/INPUT/OUTPUT prompt that proposes coordinator plus two specialist roles for the learner's own process. The EN learner's last interactive element on the whole agent track is a labeled box whose label, placeholder and copyable template are all the same meaningless string. This is unfinished authoring, not a translation choice.
reviewFindings.direction: translate the five LT fields; the `ownWorkTemplate` prompt in particular is the module's transfer artifact and must survive into EN intact, including the `{{context}}` placeholder.

reviewFindings.citation: "Optional scenarios"
reviewFindings.problem: the EN summary is a different summary, not a translation. LT section 2 recaps prompts and the Skill pack ("Įgūdžio paketas – pavadinimas, kada naudoti, rolės, žingsniai, ribos"); EN lists optional scenario flows instead. LT section 3 "Pamoka ir atnaujinimas" teaches the improvement loop (record what failed, update the rule/prompt/skill/test, retry the same edge case); EN replaces it with "Where to apply?" and application areas. The taglines diverge the same way ("…pamoka = rezultatas, kuris gerėja kitą kartą." versus "3 practices + artifacts = working result first."). The EN learner never receives the retrospective loop that LT closes the track with, and the Skill pack — a named reusable artifact produced on `124.5` — is never recapped in EN.
reviewFindings.direction: rebuild EN sections 2 and 3 from the LT text. The improvement loop and the Skill pack are the two things the LT summary is designed to leave behind; the EN "where to apply" material can stay only if it replaces something less load-bearing.

reviewFindings.citation: "\"label\": \"Scenarijai\""
reviewFindings.problem: the stat reads "Scenarijai 3" in LT and "Scenarios 4" in EN. Module 12 contains five `practice-scenario` slides (`124.5`, `124`, `121`, `122`, `123`), of which three are the required practices already counted by the adjacent stat "Privalomos praktikos 3". No reading of the module produces either 3 or 4: the extra scenarios number 2, the total is 5. Two of the three numbers on a summary slide are therefore wrong, and the two languages disagree with each other. The neighbouring `content.stats[2]` shows the same drift ("schema + įgūdis" versus "diagram + tests").
reviewFindings.direction: decide what the stat counts — extras beyond the required three, or all scenario slides — then set the same number in both languages and make the label say which. Fix `stats[2]` in the same pass.

reviewFindings.citation: "5 steps: stop, record, assess, notify, fix – slide **Testing and security**."
reviewFindings.problem: within one EN step, the description sends the learner to "Minimal workflow brief" and the hint and `partialSolution` send them to "Testing and security". The hint is the correct target (that is where the playbook lives); the description carries the same wrong pointer as LT. The EN learner gets two contradictory instructions one click apart and no way to tell which is right, while LT is uniformly wrong (A8-02).
reviewFindings.direction: make all pointers on this slide, in both languages, name the slide that actually contains the five-step playbook — after A8-01 decides whether that slide stays optional.

reviewFindings.citation: "Artefaktai: darbo eigos schema (1 p.) arba platformai paruoštas vedamasis dokumentas, nuotaikos slenksčių apibrėžimas"
reviewFindings.problem: [SOT-KONFLIKTAS] The SOT declares test cases a common artifact for all three practices ("**Bendri artefaktai visoms praktikoms:** …"), and `121` requires two while `122` requires one or two. `123` requires none — its artifact list stops at the incident playbook link. Yet the step hints still mention tests ("sugeneruok platformos specifikaciją su ChatGPT: mazgai / moduliai, slenksčiai, eskalacija, testai"), so the learner is told to produce something the acceptance criteria never ask for. The riskiest of the three bands — autonomous escalation — ends up with the weakest evidence requirement.
reviewFindings.direction: add at least one test case to the `123` artifact list (an obvious pair: a review below the threshold that escalates, and a neutral one that does not), and align the hint wording so the required and the suggested deliverables match.

reviewFindings.citation: "Trumpa lentelė arba sąrašas."
reviewFindings.problem: on `121` steps 2, 3 and 4 the `description`, `hint` and `partialSolution` are byte-identical (step 3 is the quoted sentence three times; step 4 is "Sėkmingas paleidimas + vienas klaidos atvejis." three times). `123` step 2 does the same with "Kada kurti užklausą, kokius laukus užpildyti." A learner who is stuck and asks for a hint, then asks to see a partial solution, receives the instruction they were already looking at, twice. `partialSolution` promises a worked example and delivers none. `122` shows what these fields should hold — its step 2 `partialSolution` is a full model rule with mode, condition, rejection and audit — so the pattern is available in the same module.
reviewFindings.direction: on `121` and `123`, make `hint` a nudge (what to look at, what a good answer contains) and `partialSolution` a short worked example in the learner's own domain, following the `122` step 2 model. Where no distinct value can be written, drop the field rather than echoing the description.

reviewFindings.citation: "META: [ROLĖ]. INPUT: [DUOMENYS]. OUTPUT: 1 puslapis, 3–5 punktai, lietuvių kalba."
reviewFindings.problem: the three copyables on this slide are 11–16 word skeletons in which every content slot is an unfilled bracket. The report prompt is the weakest: the body promises a multi-step chain (data → analysis → one-page report), the prompt is a single flat line with three empty placeholders and no steps, no example, no quality bar. Pasted as-is it produces a generic answer, and the learner has nothing to compare it against. Set beside the M10 slides this recap is supposed to reinforce — where `10.35` ships full architect prompts with numbered sections and `10.64` ships a complete one-page brief — the recap teaches a thinner version of the very skill it revisits.
reviewFindings.direction: keep the prompts short (this is an optional recap, so Micro class is the right ambition) but make each one a working artifact: one filled example value per placeholder, and one line naming what a good answer must contain. That is enough to make the copy-and-run loop meaningful without turning the slide into a fourth practice.

reviewFindings.citation: "Who sees, who approves, what to do if rejected."
reviewFindings.problem: LT tells the learner to reuse the rule they already generated on `10.26`, which turns a mandatory earlier slide into a supply line for this practice. EN drops the pointer and repeats the step description instead — the same sentence fills `description`, `hint` and `partialSolution`, so the EN learner loses both the cross-slide continuity and the model answer that LT provides in `partialSolution` ("Režimas – išimčių peržiūra; sąlyga – žmogui, kai klientui siunčiamas atsakymas…"). Combined with A8-04, the EN version of practice 2 has no route back to the control-rule material.
reviewFindings.direction: translate the LT hint including the slide reference, and translate the LT `partialSolution` model rule instead of echoing the description.

reviewFindings.citation: "Describe what to do if API does not respond (error handling)."
reviewFindings.problem: LT's constraints end with a hosting instruction that EN omits entirely. The sentence is marked optional, so the loss is not fatal, but it is a whole requirement present in one language and absent in the other — and it is the only place in `121` that connects the practice back to the mandatory `10.36` hosting slide. Either both languages should carry the link or neither should.
reviewFindings.direction: decide whether the hosting note belongs on `121` at all (see A8-19) and then apply the same decision to both languages.

reviewFindings.citation: "(2) What was newest? (3) What do I want to try first with a real process?"
reviewFindings.problem: LT's reflection asks what step will be applied in 24 hours, what lesson was recorded after the first test, and what will be updated — rule, prompt, skill or test. EN keeps only question 1 and replaces the other two with "what was newest" and "what to try first". The LT questions close the improvement loop the module teaches; the EN questions are generic course-feedback questions that could follow any module. Since this prompt is copyable, the difference propagates into whatever the learner does next.
reviewFindings.direction: translate the LT questions, keeping the rule/prompt/skill/test enumeration, so the reflection artifact matches the loop taught in `content.sections[2]`.

reviewFindings.citation: "Nuotaikos slenksčiai: jei < 3 žvaigždutės arba neigiamas atsiliepimas"
reviewFindings.problem: `123` gives the learner no way to check the quality of what they produced. `122` embeds a full evaluator ("VERTINTOJO PROMPTAS: Patikrink santrauką: (1) tonas tinkamas klientui…"), `121` at least has two labelled test slots in its template, and M10 closes with a mandatory evaluator slide. `123` has neither tests (A8-12) nor an evaluator, so the highest-risk practice — automated escalation on sentiment — is the only one where nobody, human or AI, checks the artifact before the learner marks it done. The threshold example is also asserted rather than reasoned: "< 3 žvaigždutės" arrives with no guidance on how to pick a threshold for a different feedback scale.
reviewFindings.direction: add a short evaluator prompt in the `122` style (does the threshold have a justification, does every escalation name an owner and a ticket field, what happens on a false positive), and one line on how to choose a threshold when the input is not a star rating.

reviewFindings.citation: "Naudok Zapier arba Make (užtenka nemokamo lygio)."
reviewFindings.problem: this single field carries four unrelated instructions: which tool to use, what to do without an account, how to describe API failures, and how to host a separate AI service with always-on or cron mode. The last one lands on a learner who is building a form-to-CRM-to-email flow, where no separate service exists; it introduces Railway, Render, always-on and cron in one clause and marks the whole thing "neprivaloma" only at the very end. This is the first mandatory practice in the module and the densest paragraph on the slide, and the operational terms arrive before the learner has any reason to need them.
reviewFindings.direction: split the field — keep tool choice and the no-account fallback in `constraints`, move error handling to where the template already asks for it, and either drop the hosting clause from this practice or move it to `123`, where a separate service is plausible.

reviewFindings.citation: "Naudok [įrankį – paieška arba skaičiuoklę] ir pateik rezultatą su trumpu paaiškinimu."
reviewFindings.problem: [SOT-KONFLIKTAS] The SOT specifies this recap prompt should produce a tool trace, and the slide body sets the learner up for exactly that ("patikrink, ar DI panaudojo įrankį atsakyme"). The prompt then never asks the AI to show which tool it used, so the check the body describes cannot be performed from the output. The learner is told to verify something the prompt does not surface.
reviewFindings.direction: have the prompt ask for the tool trace explicitly (which tool, what it returned) so the body's check has something to check.

reviewFindings.citation: "Form → Sheets/CRM → Email → Slack/Teams (Zapier or Make)"
reviewFindings.problem: LT says "lentelė" — any spreadsheet — while EN names Google Sheets specifically, and the same substitution repeats in `scenario.context` and the field-mapping step. A learner on Excel or Airtable reads the EN version as a product requirement it is not. Minor, but it recurs four times across the slide.
reviewFindings.direction: use a generic term in EN ("spreadsheet") to match LT, keeping product names for the automation platforms where they really are constrained.

reviewFindings.citation: "\"value\": \"schema + įgūdis\""
reviewFindings.problem: a summary statistic whose value is "schema + įgūdis" reads as a fragment rather than a count, and "įgūdis" here is shorthand for the Skill pack ("Įgūdžio paketas") named elsewhere on the same slide. EN shows "diagram + tests" — a different pair of artifacts again. Between the three stats the learner gets one correct number, one wrong number (A8-10) and one label they have to decode.
reviewFindings.direction: make the third stat a countable artifact figure or spell the artifact names out consistently with the vocabulary used in `content.sections[0]`, in both languages.

reviewFindings.path: src/data/glossary-en.json (compared against src/data/glossary.json) ; terms with moduleId: 10 — 8 LT terms have no EN counterpart: Always-on paleidimas, GitHub (repo), Hostingas (PaaS), Klaidos tvarkymas, Ribos (guardrails), RPA, Vartotojo promptas, Vykdymas (execution)
reviewFindings.citation: `"term": "Ribos (guardrails)",`
reviewFindings.problem: LT ships 23 M10 terms, EN ships 16. An EN learner who meets guardrails on 10.6, PaaS on 10.36, RPA on 10.35 and error handling on 10.6/10.51 finds nothing in the glossary. The lost teaching points are specific and not recoverable from other entries: the always-on vs cron vs one-shot webhook contrast, the „PaaS runs it, Zapier/n8n assembles it“ distinction, the „if an API exists choose a workflow, not RPA“ decision rule, and the user-prompt vs system-prompt separation that 10.3 depends on.
reviewFindings.direction: pack the 8 EN twins with the same `moduleId` and the same teaching point as LT; treat the four decision-rule terms (PaaS, RPA, Always-on, Vartotojo promptas) as must-have because they carry a choice, not just a label.

reviewFindings.path: src/data/glossary.json, src/data/glossary-en.json ; term "Sisteminis promptas" (moduleId: 1), rewarded by M10 path-step 10.51
reviewFindings.citation: `"term": "Sisteminis promptas",`
reviewFindings.problem: path-step 10.51 hands out `"Sisteminis promptas"` as a reward (`modules.json` → `unlockedGlossaryTerms`), but the glossary entry is tagged `moduleId: 1`, so it disappears from the Agent-path module filter on the glossary page, and `glossary-en.json` contains no `System prompt` entry at all. The EN learner is promised a term that does not exist anywhere in the EN glossary; the LT learner is sent to a Module 1 shelf. This is the central term of slide 10.3 („Rolės ir sisteminis promptas“).
reviewFindings.direction: decide one owner module for the term and make the reward list, the LT entry `moduleId` and the EN twin agree; add the missing EN entry regardless of which module wins.

reviewFindings.citation: `Lietuviškai – paleidiklis.`
reviewFindings.problem: the three workflow-core terms are stored with bare English headwords while the module teaches them in Lithuanian first — slide 10.15 says „**Paleidiklis (trigger)** → **Sąlyga (condition)** → **Veiksmas (action)**“ and the module summary repeats „Paleidiklis → Sąlyga → Veiksmas“. The definitions themselves close with „Lietuviškai – paleidiklis / veiksmas / sąlyga“, i.e. the entry admits the Lithuanian word is the real term but hides it at the end. A learner searching the alphabetical glossary for „paleidiklis“ after the slide finds nothing, and the established house pattern for exactly this case is LT-first bilingual (`Žmogaus kontrolė (Human-in-the-loop / HITL)`, `Maršrutizatorius`, `Įrankis (tool)`).
reviewFindings.direction: invert to the LT-first bilingual headword pattern already used by neighbouring entries, and let the definition carry the plain explanation instead of the language note; keep the English word visible so slide copy still matches.

reviewFindings.citation: `"slideId": 10.26`
reviewFindings.problem: GOLDEN §3.4d requires `unlockedBy` to stay in sync with the path-step `unlockedGlossaryTerms` lists. M10 path-steps award 10 terms (10.21 → Agentas (DI), Įrankis (tool), API, ReAct; 10.451 → Koordinatorius, Vertintojas, Maršrutizatorius; 10.51 → Sisteminis promptas, Klaidos tvarkymas, Trigger), but only `API` carries `unlockedBy`. The one other `unlockedBy` in the set points at 10.26, which is a content-block, not a path-step, so it records a reward the path never grants. The result is a reward mechanic that is wired for 1 of 10 terms and mis-wired for an eleventh.
reviewFindings.direction: regenerate `unlockedBy` from the path-step reward lists as the single source, and drop or re-point the 10.26 entry so no non-path-step slide claims a reward.

reviewFindings.path: src/data/glossary.json ; missing terms — "Specialistas" (M10 role), and no moduleId: 11 / moduleId: 12 terms at all
reviewFindings.citation: `"definition": "Kelių agentų rolė, kuri suskaido užduotį, paskiria specialistus ir sujungia jų rezultatus.",`
reviewFindings.problem: the module teaches four multi-agent roles and the summary lists all four („Koordinatorius, specialistas, vertintojas, maršrutizatorius“), but only three are defined; the Koordinatorius entry above even leans on „specialistams“ as if it were already defined. M12 additionally names „Įgūdžio paketas“ as a deliverable on 120.55 and 128 and never defines it. So the glossary defines the roles a learner delegates to, minus the one that does the work, and defines nothing the project module produces.
reviewFindings.direction: add `Specialistas` next to the other three roles, and decide whether the M12 project vocabulary (at minimum the skill-packet artifact) belongs in the glossary — right now the Agent path's final module has no glossary footprint.

reviewFindings.citation: `Kai API yra – rinkis workflow, ne RPA.`
reviewFindings.problem: the same sentence on the module's own glossary slide reads „Kai API yra – rinkis darbo eigą, ne RPA.“ The glossary copy keeps the raw loanword where the slide already switched to Lithuanian, so the two surfaces state the decision rule with different vocabulary. The entry for `Integracija` has the same issue („Būtinas agentams ir workflow automatizavimui“).
reviewFindings.direction: align both entries with the term the slides use for the concept; the plain-language guide allows the loanword only as a bilingual first mention, not as the standing noun.

reviewFindings.citation: `Režimą renkame pagal pasekmę`
reviewFindings.problem: the definition speaks in institutional first-person plural while the identical sentence on slide 10.7 addresses the learner directly („Režimą rink pagal pasekmę…“). Inside the same product the same rule is delivered as „what we do“ in one place and „what you do“ in the other, which weakens it from an instruction to a description.
reviewFindings.direction: keep the direct second-person instruction used on the slide so the glossary reads as guidance the learner acts on.

reviewFindings.citation: `Agentų ciklo principas: suprasti užduotį, pasirinkti įrankį, vykdyti veiksmą`
reviewFindings.problem: neither string appears anywhere in modules 10-12 outside the glossary slide itself. `ReAct` is worse than an orphan: path-step 10.21 hands it out as a reward for a step whose teaching slide (10.2) describes the cycle as „Agentas → Planavimas → Įrankiai → Aplinka → Rezultatas → Grįžtamasis ryšys“ and never names ReAct. The learner is rewarded with a label for a concept the module deliberately taught under different words.
reviewFindings.direction: either introduce the name once where the cycle is taught, or drop it from the reward list so the glossary stops promising vocabulary the module does not use.

reviewFindings.citation: `"Tikslas – įvardyk, kokį rezultatą agentas turi paruošti ir kada klausti žmogaus.",`
reviewFindings.problem: the handout's five „agent cycle“ steps are Tikslas / Kontekstas / Veiksmai / Stebėjimas / Atnaujinimas, but the module's agent cycle (10.2, and the diagram the learner clicked through) is Agentas → Planavimas → Įrankiai → Aplinka → Rezultatas → Grįžtamasis ryšys, and the glossary states it a third way under ReAct. The handout's list is actually a blend of prompt structure and the closed learning loop from 10.49 („istorija → patikra → pamokos → atnaujinimas“). The count matches, the names do not, so the takeaway sheet cannot act as a recall cue for what the learner actually saw.
reviewFindings.direction: rebuild the list from the cycle taught on 10.2 (or state plainly that this is the learning loop, not the agent cycle) so the handout and the slide reinforce one vocabulary.

reviewFindings.path: src/data/m1012HandoutContent.json, src/data/m1012HandoutContent-en.json ; workflowSteps, and the flow baked into starterPrompt
reviewFindings.citation: `"Trigger – kas pradeda procesą: forma, laiškas, lentelė, failas arba rankinis veiksmas.",`
reviewFindings.problem: the handout presents a canonical five-step flow trigger → action → tool → human gate → log, and the starter prompt hard-codes it as the required output. The module teaches a three-step core (Paleidiklis → Sąlyga → Veiksmas, drilled in the 10.485 and 10.61 self-checks and repeated in the M10 summary) and an eight-block full brief on 10.64. The handout drops Sąlyga/Condition — the single element the module quizzes most — and promotes „Tool“ and „Human gate“ to flow steps, which the slides never do. „Human gate“ and „Log“ as step labels appear nowhere in modules 10-12. Additionally, the Lithuanian handout carries these five labels in bare English while the module names them in Lithuanian.
reviewFindings.direction: reconcile to one decomposition (the 3-step core plus the named extras, or the 8-block brief) and use the Lithuanian step names in the Lithuanian handout; the starter prompt must ask for whatever flow the module actually taught.

reviewFindings.citation: `META: Tu esi agentų procesoės koordinatorius.`
reviewFindings.problem: the role line of the only copy-paste artifact on the sheet contains a corrupted word, so the learner's first pasted instruction to the model is malformed. The EN twin reads cleanly („You are an agent workflow coordinator“), which confirms this is a defect in the artifact rather than a stylistic choice. Because this is a takeaway meant to be used away from the course, nobody is present to notice and repair it.
reviewFindings.direction: repair the role line against the EN twin's meaning and keep the two starter prompts semantically identical.

reviewFindings.citation: `"Automatizuoti – taisyklėmis paremtas srautas, kai dauguma žingsnių kartojasi.",`
reviewFindings.problem: the 3A bands are described without the 80 % / 15 % / 5 % shares that the module attaches to them everywhere it teaches them (slide 120.25, the three practice titles 121/122/123, and the M10 summary line „Automatizuoti 80 % / Asistuoti 15 % / Autonomizuoti 5 %“). The proportions are the actionable part of the model — they tell the learner where most of their own processes belong — and the handout is the surface where that guidance matters most.
reviewFindings.direction: carry the band shares into the handout so the model keeps its calibrating function off-platform.

reviewFindings.citation: `schema, promptai, bandymo atvejis ir aiški žmogaus patvirtinimo vieta.`
reviewFindings.problem: the handout defines path completion with a four-item artifact list that omits the skill packet, even though M12 names it as a required output in the scenario brief („Artefaktai: schema (rolės + perdavimas), 3 promptai, 1 bandymo atvejis …, Įgūdžio paketas pakartotiniam naudojimui“) and the project summary repeats it. A learner working from the handout alone will consider the path finished one artifact early.
reviewFindings.direction: match the artifact list to the module's own definition of done, or state that the sheet lists a subset.

reviewFindings.citation: `Decide your next step (Decide)`
reviewFindings.problem: both secondary calls to action carry a trailing English tag in brackets. In EN the tag duplicates the verb of its own label word-for-word, which reads as a leftover key name rather than copy; in LT the bracket adds an English word the learner has no use for and that names nothing in the course. The bracket occupies the space where a reader deciding whether to click would expect to learn what is behind the link.
reviewFindings.direction: drop the bracketed key echoes and let each label say what the learner gets; if the two destinations need short codes, they belong in metadata, not in the visible label.

reviewFindings.citation: `Agentų orchestratoriaus modelis (blog)`
reviewFindings.problem: two mismatches with the in-product label for the same destination (`src/locales/lt.json` → `module.ecosystemDeepenM10Label` = „Agentų orkestratoriaus modelis (EN skaitinys)“). The handout spells the role differently from every other Lithuanian surface, and it replaces the „EN skaitinys“ signal with „(blog)“, so a Lithuanian reader is not warned that the destination is an English-language read before leaving the sheet.
reviewFindings.direction: use one spelling of the role across handout and locale, and keep the language warning that the in-product label already carries.

reviewFindings.citation: `Rekomenduojame peržiūrėti Modulį 10 ir pasinerti giliau į agentų vertinimą.`
reviewFindings.problem: the only agent-track string that speaks as the institution („we recommend“) instead of addressing the learner directly, which every neighbouring string does („Baigei…“, „Pasirink…“, „Patikrink savo promptą“). The EN counterpart is a plain imperative („Review Module 10 and go deeper on evaluating agents.“), so the two locales also differ in who is speaking. It sits on the post-test results screen, where a direct next step lands better than a recommendation.
reviewFindings.direction: bring it into the same direct address as the surrounding agent-track copy and match the EN imperative.

reviewFindings.citation: `"agentWorkflowEnlargeLabel": "Agentų ciklas"`
reviewFindings.problem: the same diagram label reads „Agentų ciklas“ in LT and `"agentWorkflowEnlargeLabel": "Agent workflow"` in EN. The module treats cycle and workflow as two distinct teaching objects — the agent cycle is 10.2, the workflow is 10.15 — so the EN label points the learner at the wrong concept for a diagram the LT side calls the cycle. Slide 10.2's own EN title is „Agent cycle and architecture“.
reviewFindings.direction: use the cycle wording on both sides so the enlarge control names the same object the diagram teaches.
